LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. Yes. Yes. Let me say it again: Yes. After a horror show in Week 4 with my NFL picks , I got back on track in a big way this past week. I was 10-4-1 straight up and 9-6-1 against the spread. That brings my season record straight up to 48-30-1 and the ATS record to 34-43-2. The ATS mark will be a slow climb to get back above .500 after that really bad Week 3. But I felt good about the picks this week. Time to build some momentum. Two good weeks in a row? All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Seattle Seahawks (-3) at Denver Broncos Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Seahawks lost a tough one to the 49ers last week and now face a short week on the road against Denver. The Broncos ' offense has struggled, even with Sean Payton taking over as the play-caller. Bo Nix has to pick it up, but this is a tough defense to try and fix things. Seattle takes a tough road game. Pick: Seahawks 23, Broncos 17 Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) London on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Jaguars will have been in London for two weeks, which makes this a challenge for the Texans , who went this week. Houston won for the first time on the road last week and now their division chances probably rest on this game. The Jaguars were sloppy last week, which will get them back focused. Jaguars will win a tight one. Pick: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons (+3) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a horrible showing in Green Bay, in which the defense was shredded. But the Falcons lost in overtime to the Ravens and quarterback Michael Penix was hurt. He will likely play here, and that's a good thing since he can light up the Chicago defense. Falcons win it. Pick: Falcons 27, Bears 21 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns There is a chance that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will be back for this game after missing last week with an ankle injury. Even if he isn't, I think the Ravens defense will be up to the task of slowing down the Browns offense. If Jackson is back, the Ravens offense will move the ball. Pick: Ravens 24, Browns 13 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts (-7) The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game. Pick: Colts 28, Titans 17 New York Jets at New England Patriots (-7.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Patriots have turned their season around with consecutive victories as Drake Maye has come alive. The Jets played better on defense against Cleveland last week with eight sacks, but this is a bigger challenge. Look for Maye to keep it going as the Pats win a third straight. Pick: Patriots 28, Jets 13 New Orleans Saints at New York Giants (+1.5) The Saints have lost three straight and have fallen to 1-4. They didn't play well against the Vikings last week, but this is a chance to get right. The Giants tied last week, but Jameis Winston played well. I think this will be about defenses. Giants in a close one. Pick: Giants 19, Saints 16 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense. Pick: Eagles 23, Panthers 20 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3) Both of these teams righted the ship a bit with victories last week. The Bucs badly needed it after losing their first four. Tampa Bay ran it with Bucky Irving to beat the Cowboys and I think they can do that here as well. The defense played better in that game and will limit Aaron Rodgers somewhat. Bucs win it. Pick: Bucs 26, Steelers 21 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams (-13.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The "Dream Team" Rams are 2-3 and haven't looked the part of a Super Bowl champ. The offense got it going against the Bills , but the defense was a non-factor in the fourth quarter and overtime. They will play better here against the Cardinals . Meanwhile, Matt Stafford will have a big day. Pick: Rams 35, Cardinals 20 Los Angeles Chargers (+8.5) at Kansas City Chiefs Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chargers limp into this one at 0-5, while the Chiefs are undefeated off a bye. The Chargers are desperate and need a win or their season will be over. This is not a good place to try to get that first victory. Look for Patrick Mahomes to play well. Chiefs coach Andy Reid is outstanding in his career off a bye. Pick: Chiefs 28, Chargers 21 Buffalo Bills (-6) at Las Vegas Raiders The Bills are playing consecutive road games, but they stayed on the West Coast after beating the Rams in overtime Monday night. That was a tough, physical game, which will make it a challenge on a short week. The Raiders were awful against the Pats, but they will play better on offense here. They just won't stop the Bills. Pick: Bills 35, Raiders 21 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Packers blew out the Bears Sunday as Jordan Love lit up the skies. Look for more of that in this one against a bad Dallas secondary. The Cowboys struggled on defense against the Bucs, and that will continue in this one. Love continues to play well. Packers win a shootout. Pick: Packers 31, Cowboys 27 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a long road trip for the Commanders off a brutal tie last week to face the league's best team right now. That's a tough combination. They can only hope for a letdown by the 49ers after they beat Seattle last week. It won't happen. The 49ers continue to roll as Brock Purdy continues to make a claim as a legitimate MVP candidate. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) at Denver Broncos (TNF) Dajani ( Seahawks -2.5): Through five weeks, I have only bet against the Denver Broncos once. It's an uncomfortable position to be in, since Bo Nix is "captain comeback." For example, I had zero doubt they would come back from down 16-0 against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 3. Denver has the most comeback wins (15), second-half comebacks (12) and fourth-quarter comebacks (8) in the NFL since 2025. However, I'm going to fade the Broncos in this spot for a couple of reasons. One, Sean Payton taking back play-calling duties did not help anything against the Los Angeles Chargers . Getting this offense off the ground is, unfortunately, going to take some time -- and it probably won't happen against the No. 1 defense in the NFL. Secondly, the Seahawks have to be mad after that loss to the 49ers. Seattle has won five straight games following a loss, having not lost back-to-back games since 2024. The Seahawks have also won seven straight prime-time games, which is the longest active streak in the NFL. … Prediction: Seahawks 23, Broncos 20 Dubin (Seahawks -2.5): Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have resulted in the Broncos coming away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Patrick Surtain II here, which is obviously a problem against Jaxon Smith-Njigba . … Prediction: Seahawks 24, Broncos 16 Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. But the numbers beneath those records leave room for a considerably less predictable afternoon in London. Jacksonville enters as a 2.5-point favorite after escaping Philadelphia 19-17. Houston finally broke through by beating Tennessee 26-3, then acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. These predictions deliberately push beyond a narrow upset or another respectable quarterback performance. The forecast: Houston produces its most complete game of the season. CJ Stroud throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Jacksonville's defense allows only 14 points per game, second in the NFL. Predicting four passing touchdowns against that unit is aggressive, but its strength against the run can obscure a vulnerable pass defense. Conversely, they allow an NFL-best 63.8 rushing yards per game and just 2.9 yards per carry. Houston therefore has good reason to attack through Stroud rather than repeatedly challenge Jacksonville's strongest area. Stroud has already thrown for 1,402 yards with six touchdowns and no interceptions through five games. Against Tennessee, he completed 26 of 34 attempts for 261 yards, including an impressive eight completions on 11 pressured throws for 115 yards. The prediction requires Houston to convert passing volume into touchdowns, something it has not consistently accomplished. Harrison's arrival creates another possible weapon, although his debut and workload remain uncertain. This call rests primarily on Stroud's existing production and Jacksonville's passing-yardage vulnerability, not an assumption that the newcomer immediately dominates. Will Anderson Jr. records four sacks as Houston forces three turnovers Anderson delivered three of Houston's four sacks against Tennessee, providing the foundation for an even bigger prediction against Jacksonville. Four sacks by one player would be a spectacular follow-up, not merely continued improvement. The Texans limited the Titans to 187 total yards and three points after DeMeco Ryans reclaimed defensive play-calling duties. Tennessee's struggling offense makes that result an imperfect measuring stick, but Houston still ranks ninth in yards allowed per play. Jacksonville presents a tougher opponent, yet Sunday exposed pressure points. Trevor Lawrence threw an interception and lost a fumble against Philadelphia despite producing 331 passing yards and two touchdowns. Houston must turn disruptive plays into possession changes, rather than simply allowing Jacksonville to reset after sacks. The Jaguars' penalty problems could help create those opportunities. They have committed at least 13 penalties and accumulated more than 100 penalty yards in consecutive games. Backward movement makes passing situations more predictable, giving Anderson additional chances to attack. The bold call is four Anderson sacks and three Houston takeaways: pressure converts Jacksonville's mistakes into decisive field-position advantages. The Texans win by at least 17 points Jacksonville's winning record and scoring defense make a comfortable Houston victory the biggest leap here. The Jaguars have allowed only 70 points across five games, while the Texans entered last Sunday without a win. Nevertheless, a blowout becomes plausible if the first two predictions connect. Houston's passing offense attacks Jacksonville's statistical weakness, while turnovers supply short fields and prevent Lawrence from answering every score. Jacksonville also needed a 53-yard kickoff return and Cam Little's 57-yard field goal to escape Philadelphia. That extraordinary finish demonstrated resilience, but it should not conceal how close the Jaguars came to losing. Stroud's four touchdown passes power the offense, and defensive disruption keeps the Jaguars from turning their rushing balance into sustained control. London delivers a division-changing upset, not another last-second escape. The Texans are coming off their first win while the Jags take the field following their most unlikely win of the season. A preseason favorite of many to contend for the Super Bowl, Houston finally got into the win column last week with an impressive 26-3 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Nashville. For the first time this season, the highly touted Texans dominated defensively, limiting Tennessee to just three points and 187 Total Yards. C.J. Stroud connected on passes to seven different receivers and threw for 261 yards to lead the attack on offense. Jacksonville, meanwhile, won a game they may not have deserved but were glad to have been gifted. They knocked off the Eagles, 19-17, at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Philadelphia took the lead with eight seconds remaining. Jacksonville was without a timeout, but Ameer Abdullah managed to return the ensuing kickoff 53 yards in seven seconds. Cam Little then converted a 57-yard field goal as time expired to win the game for the Jags. Jacksonville has now won three straight. They lead the AFC South by two games over the Colts and three games over the Texans. Stroud and the Texans have moved the ball through the air (No. 4 in the NFL with 1402 yards), but only Green Bay has gained fewer yards on the ground (No. 31 with 395 yards). Couple that disparity with an issue turning yardage into points – they have scored as a team just 11 touchdowns this season – and the 1-4 start is not all that surprising. Jacksonville’s fast start is based on the defensive side of the ball. The Jags allow yards but not points. They are the No. 2 scoring defense in the league allowing just 70 points through five games. home.headline: Jaguars turn to Jacob Bobenmoyer after Ross Matiscik injury: Report
home.blurb: This story was updated to add new information. The Jacksonville Jaguars have found a replacement for defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton , who served as the team's long snapper for most of Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles in London. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday that the long snapper was arriving shortly, and he's now at The Grove with the rest of the team. According to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport, the Jaguars will sign veteran long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer , while typical starting long snapper Ross Matiscik recovers from a shoulder injury sustained in the first quarter against Philly. Who is long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer, Ross Matiscik's replacement? Bobenmoyer, 29, has spent seven years in the NFL with two teams: the Denver Broncos (2019-2022) and the Las Vegas Raiders (2023-2025). Bobenmoyer has played 97 games, recording 22 tackles and 1 fumble recovery. Jacksonville is currently overseas in London as it prepares to play its second of two matchups across the pond. The Jaguars will take on the Houston Texans in Week 6. According to Rapoport, Bobenmoyer has already flown to London. Hamilton stepped in for Jacksonville after Matiscik was injured. Teams typically carry only one long snapper on their 53-man roster or practice squad. Sunday's win marked the second time Hamilton served as the team's long snapper after Matiscik's injury. Hamilton helped set up Cam Little 's game-winning 57-yard field goal . Although Hamilton's snap was high, punter Logan Cooke got the ball down quickly, giving Little time to boot it through the uprights. The Jaguars won in the final seconds against the Eagles, 19-17. The Jaguars (4-1) will face off against the Texans in Week 6 at Wembley Stadium as they look to bury their division rival. The Texans are currently 1-4 after netting their first win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 5. Demetrius Harvey is the Jacksonville Jaguars reporter for the Florida Times-Union. A limited participation in practice is a great sign that his return is right around the corner. However, he might still be ruled inactive for Week 6 against the Jaguars if unable to complete a full practice. If that's the case, Jake Hansen will remain Houston's fill in as their WLB. Another aspect of the Texans' injury report that can't go unnoticed: wide receiver Tank Dell has participated in his first full practice since being designated to return from his knee injury suffered back in 2024. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Sam Householder Thu, October 15, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears look to rebound from an ugly, humiliating loss to the Green Bay Packers while going on the road for the second straight week. This time, they should get starting QB Caleb Williams back. But he's going to have a fight on his hands. The Atlanta Falcons have an explosive offense with stars Drake London and Bijan Robinson. Robinson is making a case for being one of, if not the , best running back in the league. Certainly among elite company like Kenneth Walker III, Jahmyr Gibbs, Derrick Henry and James Cook. Michael Penix Jr., the quarterback taken seven spots after Williams, is a great facilitator for Kevin Stefanski's offense. He looks set to play despite a rib injury suffered late against the Ravens last week. Penix's biggest issue over his first three seasons has been availability. Sunday will be his 16th start and 18th overall game. Let's dive a little deeper into the Falcons and their history against Chicago. Atlanta Falcons SB Nation site : The Falcoholic Record: 2-3, second in the NFC South Last week: 30-23 loss in OT to the Ravens Game day, time, TV: Sunday, noon CT, FOX Spread: Bears -1.5 Bears all-time record against: 16-14 Historical meetings: The Bears and Falcons met in week 6 of the 2013 season with both teams at 2-3. The teams traded field goals, but Chicago found the end zone first with a 3-yard pass to Josh Morgan from Jay Cutler. This game ended up being a Bears-career high in passing yards for Cutler. He threw for 381 yards but just one touchdown. However, they had two 100-yard receiving games from Brandon Marshall (113) and Alshon Jeffery (136). Matt Forte rushed for two touchdowns. A late Matt Ryan interception helped seal it and the Bears won 27-13. Last meeting: Remember when there was very brief excitement that Matt Eberflus was building something? Week 17 of the 2023 season, the Bears moved to 7-9 when they stomped the Falcons 37-17 at Soldier Field. Taylor Heinicke threw three interceptions and was eventually benched for Desmond Ridder, who also threw a pick. Justin Fields threw a touchdown to DJ Moore, who had 159 yards. Fields also rushed for a touchdown, along with Khalil Herbert and Roschon Johnson. Herbert also had 124 yards. Injury report: The Falcons had three players on their Wednesday injury report. Did not participate CB C.J. Henderson (groin) Limited participation LB Divine Deablo (hamstring) DE Za'Darius Smith (concussion/neck) Offense: The Falcons offense ranks 13th in points and 10th in yards. Their rushing offense ranks second and their passing offense ranks 21st. The Falcons have gotten hot offensively since Michael Penix (67.5 pct. cmp./719 yds./3 TD/1 INT) came back. It helps to have Bijan Robinson (102 att./580 yds./4 TD), who leads the league in rushing. And Drake London (27 rec./488 yds./0 TD), who averages 18.1 yards per reception but somehow has no touchdowns. Bijan (18 rec./152 yds./1 TD) is actually their second-leading receiver. Followed by TE Kyle Pitts (10/109/1) and Jahan Dotson (8/149/1). Austin Hooper (5/40/1), Zachariah Branch (7/46/0) and former Bear Olamide Zaccheaus (4/17/0) are also role players. Behind Bijan is the other B. Robinson, Brian (51/210/4), who gets a fair share of carries inside the red zone. Defense: The Falcons defense ranks 21st in points and 16th in yards. Their rushing defense ranks fourth and their passing defense ranks 27th. S Xavier Watts (34 tkl/1 INT/2 PD/1 FF), LB Divine Deablo (16 tkls/1 PD/1 TFL/2 QB hits), CB Mike Hughes (25 tkls/1 TFL/3 PD) and CB C.J. Henderson (25 tkls/1 TFL/6 PD/1 FF) are the tackling leaders. S Jessie Bates III (24 tkls/2 PD/1 FR) and Za'Darius Smith (2.5 sk/4 TFL/3 QB hits) are two of the bigger names on the unit, but there is plenty of talent elsewhere, too. Cameron Thomas (2 sk/10 QB hits/1 TFL/1 FF) and Samson Ebukam (2.5 sk/9 QB hits/2 TFL) are among the leading pass-rushers. Gervon Dexter (0.5 sk/2 TFL/3 QB hits) is making himself comfortable in Atlanta's defensive scheme, too. Key matchups: The defense is going to have its hands full with Atlanta's playmakers. Bijan is tough for any team to contain. Combine him with London, who is a threat all over the field, and Dennis Allen's unit will have its hands full. Until last week's Ravens game, the Falcons have held opponents' rushing attack in check. It was opponents' aerial attacks that were doing damage. Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams will have to find the right balance to keep the Bears on the field, minimize Atlanta's time of possession, while scoring as many points as they can. The Bears can hang in a shootout, but Chicago will want the ball last. The Falcons' offense has turned the ball over in four of their five games. Atlanta has allowed nine passing touchdowns to three rushing touchdowns. The nine passing TD is tied for the fifth-most in the league. Opponents have the second-most pass attempts in the league against Atlanta, behind only Detroit. Atlanta has just one interception on the season, as well. The Falcons offense has the second-fewest pass attempts in the league and the second-most rushing attempts. While Chicago's red zone offensive woes are well-documented, Atlanta ranks seventh in offensive red zone scoring, getting in 69.2 percent of their trips.

picks.blurb: Bears vs. Falcons Preview: Chicago Looks to Bounce Back Against Atlanta - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers to advance to World Series TRENDING Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Bears vs. Falcons Preview: Chicago Looks to Bounce Back Against Atlanta Photo by: Brett Davis Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:05 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears travel to Mercedes Benz Stadium on Sunday to face the Atlanta Falcons in a Week 6 matchup featuring two teams looking to respond after disappointing losses. Chicago enters the game at 3-2 after suffering a 31-7 defeat against the Green Bay Packers. Atlanta is 2-3 following a heartbreaking 30-23 overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens. Both teams need a strong performance as they look to build momentum in their respective divisions. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Caleb Williams' Potential Return Could Boost Chicago One of the biggest storylines heading into Sunday's matchup is the status of Bears quarterback Caleb Williams . Williams has been sidelined with a hamstring injury since Week 2, leaving backup quarterback Tyson Bagent to lead the offense. Chicago struggled against Green Bay, managing only seven points in a difficult road loss. Williams' potential return could provide a major boost. His ability to extend plays, attack defenses downfield and create opportunities outside the pocket would give Chicago another dimension offensively. Running back D'Andre Swift will also be important. Swift has been a productive part of the Bears' offense, and establishing the running game could help Chicago control possession and take pressure off its quarterback. Head coach Ben Johnson will need his offense to play with greater consistency after the struggles against Green Bay. Michael Penix Jr. Leads Atlanta's Offense The Falcons also have a quarterback storyline of their own. Michael Penix Jr. is expected to return as Atlanta's starter after suffering a rib injury during the loss to Baltimore. Penix has completed 67.5% of his passes for 719 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in three starts this season. His availability will be important for an Atlanta offense that features several dangerous playmakers. Running back Bijan Robinson has been one of the Falcons' most productive players, combining explosive rushing ability with his contributions as a receiver. Wide receiver Drake London is another major threat, giving Penix a reliable target capable of making difficult catches and creating big plays. Head coach Kevin Stefanski will look to get the offense back on track after the Falcons let a late lead slip away against Baltimore. Defensive Matchups Could Decide the Game Chicago will need to contain Robinson and prevent Atlanta from controlling the game on the ground. If the Bears can force Penix into obvious passing situations, their defense could create opportunities for turnovers. Atlanta, meanwhile, must prepare for the possibility of Williams returning. The Falcons will need to pressure the quarterback while limiting Swift's opportunities to break through the defensive front. A Crucial Week 6 Test Both teams have reasons to view Sunday's matchup as an opportunity to respond. Chicago needs a better offensive performance after its loss to Green Bay, while Atlanta wants to turn its competitive play into victories. With Williams potentially returning and Penix expected to lead the Falcons, quarterback play could be the defining storyline. The team that protects the football, establishes its running game and executes in key moments will put itself in a strong position in this Week 6 showdown.

away.headline: Lions sign former Bears, Chargers return man after Tom Kennedy injury
away.blurb: With wide receiver and return specialist Tom Kennedy ruled out for the remainder of the season because of a knee injury , the Detroit Lions have turned to veteran return specialist DeAndre Carter to bolster their depth. Detroit signed Carter to its practice squad after working him out on Thursday, per NFL insider Tom Pelissero. The move came as the team assessed other potential options, including wide receiver and returner Steven Sims, to help fill the gap. Kennedy suffered an MCL injury during the Lions’ win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 5 and is expected to undergo surgery, ending his 2026 campaign. Before going down, the 30-year-old handled all of Detroit’s punt returns and shared kickoff-return responsibilities with Jacob Saylors. He averaged 13.2 yards per punt return, ranking sixth in the NFL, and 24.8 yards per kickoff return this season. Across his eight-year NFL career, Carter has recorded 155 punt returns for 1,508 yards, averaging 9.7 yards per attempt. He has also returned 144 kickoffs for 3,399 yards, an average of 23.6 yards, and scored a 101-yard touchdown on a kickoff return. Carter’s arrival could help the Lions reduce their reliance on offensive starters in the return game. Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown handled punt-return duties following Kennedy’s injury. Running back Jacob Saylors remains an option on kickoffs. Head coach Dan Campbell had indicated that the team would explore outside options to replace Kennedy. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Carter, 33, brings a wealth of NFL experience. The Sacramento State product went undrafted in 2015 and has played for multiple franchises. After spending time with several teams early in his career, he earned opportunities with the Philadelphia Eagles and Houston Texans in 2018. His subsequent stops included the Chicago Bears, Washington Commanders, Los Angeles Chargers, Las Vegas Raiders and Cleveland Browns. Carter appeared in four games for the Browns during the 2025 season before a knee injury led to his placement on injured reserve in late September. He has not appeared in an NFL game this season. Although primarily known for his work on special teams, Carter has also contributed on offense. He has accumulated 117 receptions for 1,331 yards and six touchdowns, along with 16 rushing attempts for 99 yards in 111 games. His best receiving season came with the Chargers in 2021, when he caught 36 passes for 538 yards. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. away.headline: Bears Thursday injury report: Caleb Williams full participant again
away.blurb: Following a walkthrough on Wednesday, the Bears practiced for the first time this week, and there was encouraging news as quarterback Caleb Williams practiced in full for the second straight day. Williams is on track to return to the starting lineup this weekend after missing the last three games with a hammering injury. Cornerback Kyler Gordon could also be gearing up for a return, as he was once again a full participant. Unfortunately, linebacker T.J. Edwards (hamstring), running back Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) and defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo were both listed as non-participants. away.headline: Bears Thursday Injury Report: Kyle Monangai in Serious Doubt, Caleb Williams Still on Track
away.blurb: After an estimated injury report on Wednesday , the Chicago Bears put out a real one on Thursday and it offered more good news for Caleb Williams, but more bad news for Kyle Monangai. For the first time since his injury, Williams logged a legitimate full practice for the Bears on Thursday, which continues to keep him on track to return in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons. Williams' return will be a huge lift for Chicago coming off a terrible loss to the Green Bay Packers that saw both Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum struggle. DB Tyrique Stevenson (hip): Limited participation Two straight days of full practice means Williams is well on his way to making his return in Week 6. In fact, it would be shocking if he doesn't play at this point. As is the case with Monangai, T.J. Edwards and Keyshaun Elliott look like they are heading for an absence this week. It would be Elliott's second straight if he is ruled out. Odeyingbo was also among the non-participants again, but we already know the veteran is likely to miss time , Ben Johnson said. In the secondary, Stevenson is looking like a slightly better than 50/50 proposition to play, and Gordon continues to practice fully, something he has been doing since being designated to return. Unfortunately, the news wasn't as good for Monangai. Here's the latest on him and more from the Bears' Thursday injury report. DL Grady Jarrett (rest): Did not participate OL Joe Thuney (rest): Did not participate LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring): Did not participate LB Keyshaun Elliott (quad): Did not participate RB Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe): Did not participate DL Dayo Odeyingbo (quad): Did not participate DB Kyler Gordon: Full participation QB Caleb Williams: Full participation The only difference from Wednesday are the additions of Thuney and Jarrett, but their absences were just rest-related, so no concerns there. The fact that Monangai was not able to take part in practice yet again is a clear indication he's in serious trouble of missing another game. It'll be interesting to see how the Bears replace Monangai if he can't play once again. Roschon Johnson was not good beind D'Andre Swift last week and perhaps the Bears should be considering either Zavier Scott or Salvon Ahmed. That would suggest Gordon will play in Week 6, but Johnson did hint the Bears could take all 21 days of his window before activating him. The Bears will drop their final injury report of the week on Friday, complete with designations. home.headline: Legendary Falcons' DT Grady Jarrett Returns to Atlanta With The Chicago Bears
home.blurb: On Sunday, just a week after the Falcons ’ legendary defensive end, John Abraham, entered the Ring of Honor , another defensive legend will return to play against the Falcons. Defensive tackle Grady Jarrett will play his first game against his hometown and former team, the Atlanta Falcons. Until last season, Jarrett had spent his entire career in his home city of Atlanta. He was drafted out of Clemson in the fifth round in 2015. Atlanta also selected fellow defensive player linebacker Vic Beasley Jr. with the eighth overall pick. Jarrett was seen as an undersized defensive tackle with short arms and was underestimated in his first few seasons. He grew to be a cornerstone type player, even earning his own radio call of “You shall not pass!” for his stout, defensive play and high football IQ. Jarrett was known for blowing up offensive plays through the middle of the defensive line, running down running backs for tackles for loss and, probably his most underrated skill, getting to the quarterback. For a tackle whose knock on him was short. Arms, being compared to future Hall of Fame tackle Aaron Donald , it was a major accomplishment. Part of what gave him his reputation as a quarterback hunter was his outstanding performance in Super Bowl 51 . In only his second season in the NFL, he sacked New England Patriots quarterback Tom Brady three times in the first half. That ties him for the most sacks by a player in a Super Bowl. That season, and that game in particular, put Jarrett on the map as a defensive interior lineman and into Pro Bowl conversations. Unfortunately for Jarrett and the Falcons, that Super Bowl would be the most meaningful game of his era. Unwilling to endure another rebuild or to restructure his contract, Jarrett was released in the 2025 offseason, allowing him to sign a lucrative contract with the Bears . Falcons fans used to seeing Jarrett at #97 will have to look for #50 on Sunday to give him the reception he deserves, but they also need to recognize who’s terrorizing Michael Penix Jr. As much as Atlanta wants to get the win on Sunday, a great reception for Jarrett after an amazing ten years of service is to be expected.

home.headline: Optimistic Caleb Williams Injury Update Boosts Bears' Odds vs. Falcons in NFL Week 6
home.blurb: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has not played since Week 2 with a Grade 2 hamstring strain, but he was listed as questionable for Week 5 against the Green Bay Packers before sitting out. Now, it appears Williams is on track to play in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons, even though there have been conflicting reports about his health over the last week. NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported on Monday that "all signs" point to the former No. 1 overall pick making his return on Sunday. Chicago's first practice report will come out on Wednesday, and if Williams is limited or a full participant, it will bode well for his chances of playing in Week 6. Chicago went from a 1.5-point underdog in the opening odds for this game to a three-point favorite, and it's now -120 to cover the spread. That's a sign that this line could move to 3.5 before Sunday's game, especially if Williams is ruled in. DraftKings Sportsbook has the Bears set at -175 to win this game outright over an Atlanta team that fell to 2-3 in Week 5. According to DraftKings, 61 percent of the moneyline bets are on the Bears while 55 percent of the spread bets are on Atlanta to cover. The Bears are 2-1 this season without the former No. 1 overall pick, but he's by far their best option at quarterback after Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum led the team to just seven points in a Week 5 loss to Green Bay. Before going down in Week 2 against the Minnesota Vikings Williams threw for 407 yards, two scores and one pick while also adding a pair of touchdowns on the ground for Chicago. Bagent has thrown three interceptions in his two starts for Chicago while Keenum threw a pick in relief of Bagent on Sunday. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) at Denver Broncos (TNF) Dajani ( Seahawks -2.5): Through five weeks, I have only bet against the Denver Broncos once. It's an uncomfortable position to be in, since Bo Nix is "captain comeback." For example, I had zero doubt they would come back from down 16-0 against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 3. Denver has the most comeback wins (15), second-half comebacks (12) and fourth-quarter comebacks (8) in the NFL since 2025. However, I'm going to fade the Broncos in this spot for a couple of reasons. One, Sean Payton taking back play-calling duties did not help anything against the Los Angeles Chargers . Getting this offense off the ground is, unfortunately, going to take some time -- and it probably won't happen against the No. 1 defense in the NFL. Secondly, the Seahawks have to be mad after that loss to the 49ers. Seattle has won five straight games following a loss, having not lost back-to-back games since 2024. The Seahawks have also won seven straight prime-time games, which is the longest active streak in the NFL. … Prediction: Seahawks 23, Broncos 20 Dubin (Seahawks -2.5): Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have resulted in the Broncos coming away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Patrick Surtain II here, which is obviously a problem against Jaxon Smith-Njigba . … Prediction: Seahawks 24, Broncos 16 Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for the Browns in Week 6 against the Ravens
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for the Browns in Week 6 against the Ravens - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers to advance to World Series TRENDING Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team 3 Bold Predictions for the Browns in Week 6 against the Ravens Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 2:04 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns are coming off their first loss since Week 1 as they head into Week 6. They are now 3-2 and have a pivotal matchup with the Baltimore Ravens on the horizon in what has now become a must-win game for them. The Browns can only control what they can control, and in Week 6 that is going to be more important than ever. The Ravens have been dealing with several injuries, including the most notable one regarding Lamar Jackson. Whether he plays or not, this defense needs to prepare the way they know how to. On offense, Todd Monken and Deshaun Watson have to find that spark again after losing the momentum they had been building. Without doing both of those things, this could be a major setback for the season as a whole. With that said, we have our eyes on three matchups within this game that we want to highlight. Carson Schwesinger vs. Lamar Jackson Carson Schwesinger has played at an All-Pro level this year, but he is dealing with an ankle injury. Also dealing with an ankle injury is Lamar Jackson. Neither man is likely to be 100%, so who will have the willpower to overcome the other? Schwesinger has been really flashing his pass-rush presence in 2026, which will help contain Lamar Jackson, but he also has just done a tremendous job patrolling the middle of the field. He will have to be on his A game against one of the best players of this generation. Denzel Ward vs. Zay Flowers Denzel Ward is quietly having one of the best seasons of his career, just as Zay Flowers is. The Browns cornerback has allowed an average of just 20 yards to players he is covering in 2026. On the flip side, Zay Flowers is averaging 97.3 yards per game, something has to give, right? Flowers has been pretty well contained in his career against the Browns, but every matchup is a fresh start. Whoever wins this matchup between two proverbial titans could tip the scales in their team's favor. Todd Monken vs. Jessee Minter Todd Monken will be playing against the team he left to become a head coach this offseason. He is familiar with the Ravens, Lamar Jackson, Zay Flowers, and everyone on that offense, so what will he be able to do to help Mike Rutenberg and his defense? On the flip side, Jesse Minter is looking to continue the hot start to his coaching career as the Ravens themselves are sitting pretty at 4-1. These coaches seem poised to face each other for years, but the first matchup will perhaps be the most interesting. The update comes after Jackson suffered an ankle injury during Baltimore’s Week 4 victory over the Tennessee Titans. Jackson exited the game at halftime and did not return, leaving backup quarterback Tyler Huntley to finish the contest. The Ravens held on for a 24-18 victory, but Jackson’s injury immediately raised concerns about how long Baltimore might be without its two-time NFL MVP. Those concerns increased when Jackson missed practice the following week and was eventually ruled out against Atlanta. Although the Ravens would welcome his return, Huntley has helped keep the team moving in his absence. away.headline: Zay Flowers, Mike Green added to Ravens' Thursday injury report
away.blurb: The Ravens added Zay Flowers and Mike Green to their injury report Thursday, while Lamar Jackson remained sidelined ahead of Sunday's AFC North matchup against the Browns . Flowers was listed as limited with a toe injury, and Green with a hamstring injury. Neither appeared on Wednesday's report, giving Baltimore two additional situations to monitor before its trip to Cleveland. Jackson was listed as a nonparticipant for the second consecutive day with an ankle injury. Rashod Bateman (shoulder), John Simpson (groin), and Broderick Washington (ankle) moved from limited participation Wednesday to nonparticipation Thursday. Tight end Matthew Hibner remained a nonparticipant with a hand injury. Jackson's absence keeps Tyler Huntley in line for another start if the two-time MVP cannot return. Coach Jesse Minter has said Jackson could play without practicing, and Thursday's report does not establish his game status. There were encouraging developments elsewhere. Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf), Roger Rosengarten (knee), Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and Nick Vannett (knee) improved from limited to full participation. Calais Campbell also returned to full participation following Wednesday's rest day. Trey Hendrickson (finger), Kyle Hamilton (stinger), Mark Andrews (hand) and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) remained full participants. Lane is designated to return from injured reserve; full participation alone does not establish that he has been activated. Center Cam Jurgens remained limited with a concussion as he works toward his Ravens debut. Teddye Buchanan, Emery Jones Jr., Trenton Simpson and Andrew Vorhees also remained limited. Baltimore enters Sunday at 4-1, one game ahead of Cleveland. Friday's practice and game designations will help determine whether the Ravens can get Jackson back and how many of their other injured players will be available for the division matchup. away.headline: Ravens Linked to Dolphins' Former 11.5-Sack Edge Rusher as Baltimore's Pass Rush Stalls at 10 Sacks
away.blurb: Baltimore’s sacks have been spread thin. Tavius Robinson leads the team with three, Mike Green has two, and Hendrickson had one in three games before the injury. Green had his best day in the overtime win at Atlanta, with a sack, two quarterback hits and two tackles for loss, but no Ravens rusher has more than three sacks. Head coach Jesse Minter sounded hopeful Monday that his top edge rusher could return against the Browns. Trey Hendrickson’s Potential Return Could Be Disastrous For Browns Offensive Line The Baltimore Ravens are 4-1 and atop the AFC North, but they’ve gotten there without much heat on opposing quarterbacks. With Trey Hendrickson sidelined by a finger injury the last two weeks, Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay pointed Baltimore toward a pass rusher who once had 11.5 sacks in a season: Miami Dolphins edge Josh Uche. Kay proposed sending a 2027 sixth-round pick to the winless Dolphins for Uche in his one trade for each of the NFL’s best teams . He noted that the Ravens are generating pressure on about 20.2% of plays, with a 5.52% sack rate and 10 sacks through five games. Josh Uche is playing like a starter again Uche’s best year came with the Patriots in 2022, when he had 11.5 sacks. He bounced from New England to Kansas City to Philadelphia over the next three seasons before signing a one-year deal in Miami, and he’s been productive there. PFF grades Uche 33rd of 106 edge defenders with a 71.7 overall mark, and he has 10 pressures on 111 pass-rush snaps. He also has 20 tackles, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. “I think Trey will be chomping at the bit to be ready to roll this week,” Minter said during his Monday news conference . Even with Hendrickson back, Uche would give Baltimore another rusher to rotate in. The cost is minimal. He’s on a one-year, $1.4 million deal with a $1.215 million base salary, and the Ravens have about $2.4 million in cap space, per Over the Cap . For a team that wants M&T Bank Stadium rocking in January, a sixth-round pick for a 28-year-old rusher is an easy call to make before the Nov. 10 deadline. Gilberto Manzano correctly bet on the Green Bay Packers to upset the Chicago Bears, and yours truly bet on the San Francisco 49ers to beat the Seattle Seahawks. We move on to the Week 6 slate, and three writers have their upset picks locked in. Let's dive into them. Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 6 Upset Pick Houston Texans (+120) vs. Jacksonville Jaguars First, let me pat myself on the back for finally getting an upset pick correctly. Now that I’ve regained your trust after my Packers-over-Bears pick came to fruition last week, do yourself a favor and take the new-look Texans over the London Jaguars. Houston gained confidence from beating up on Tennessee and landing wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with Arizona. C.J. Stroud tends to play at his best when Nico Collins is on the field, but now he doesn’t have to lock in on him with the arrival of Harrison, who played with Stroud at Ohio State. More importantly, the Texans’ defense is back on track, and that could present trouble for the inconsistent Trevor Lawrence. Iain MacMillan Week 6 Upset Pick Tennessee Titans (+260) vs. Indianapolis Colts It's time for the Titans to get their first win of the season. You might be surprised to find out how many metrics these two teams rank similarly in, even some that the Titans outrank the Colts in, like net yards per play, which has the Titans at -0.7 and the Colts second-last in the NFL at -1.6. Another interesting metric for this game is that the Titans have the second-highest run frequency in neutral game states, meaning on early downs in the middle of the game when they still have a more than 20% win probability, Tennessee loves to run the football. That could be an area they exploit in this game, as the Colts rank dead last in the NFL in opponent rush EPA and 30th in opponent run success rate. Meanwhile, the Titans rank 16th and 11th in those two run defense categories, which will go a long way in slowing down Jonathan Taylor, which is the key to beating this Colts team. I'll take Tennessee as my upset pick of the week. Peter Dewey Week 6 Upset Pick Carolina Panthers (-105) vs. Philadelphia Eagles This isn’t the craziest upset pick in Week 6 – Carolina is just a 1.5-point underdog – but I can’t pass up a chance to fade this Philadelphia offense. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are dealing with soft-tissue injuries, and the Eagles currently rank 30th in EPA/Play, 31st in success rate and 31st in yards per play this season. Only the Tennessee Titans (0-5) are averaging fewer yards per play than Philly. I think there’s a real chance that Bryce Young and this Carolina offense (eighth in EPA/Play, sixth in EPA/Pass and fifth in yards per play) put up too many points for this Eagles team to compete. After all, the Eagles are 17th in yards per play allowed on defense and 22nd in both EPA/Play and success rate. Both of those advanced numbers are behind the Panthers’ defense this season. If the Eagles didn’t enter the season with playoff expectations, I think they’d be underdogs on Sunday based on their statistical profile in 2026. Plus, Carolina is coming off a bye while the Eagles have a tough travel week coming from London. All signs point to a Panthers upset in Week 6. We have seen very little so far to give us any indication that such a spot exists. The day after the Titans get embarrassed by the Texans someone usually gets fired. Tennessee enters Week 6 at 0-5 after suffering a disappointing 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans. Indianapolis is 2-3 following a 34-22 defeat against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Both teams are looking to respond, but the Titans desperately need their first victory of the season. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Cam Ward Looks to Spark Tennessee's Offense Titans quarterback Cam Ward remains the centerpiece of Tennessee's rebuilding effort. Despite the team's winless start, head coach Robert Saleh has continued to express confidence in the young quarterback and his ability to develop. Ward has completed 63.2% of his passes for 896 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions through five games. However, the Titans have struggled to generate consistent offense, scoring just three points against Houston last week. Tennessee needs Ward to make quicker decisions, protect the football and find ways to connect with his receivers downfield. Running back Tony Pollard will also be important. Establishing a productive ground game could take pressure off Ward and help Tennessee control possession against Indianapolis. Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor Lead Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones will look to guide Indianapolis back into the win column after the loss to Pittsburgh. Jones has thrown for 1,021 yards and three touchdowns this season, although four interceptions have contributed to some of the team's offensive inconsistency. Against Tennessee, protecting the football and taking advantage of scoring opportunities will be essential. The Colts also have one of the league's most dangerous running backs in Jonathan Taylor . Taylor has recorded 398 rushing yards and six touchdowns through five games, giving Indianapolis a reliable option to control the tempo. Wide receiver Josh Downs and tight end Tyler Warren provide Jones with additional receiving threats. Head coach Shane Steichen will look to create a balanced offensive attack that allows Taylor to establish the run while opening opportunities for Jones through the air. Can Tennessee Slow Down the Colts? The Titans' defense must find a way to contain Taylor and prevent Indianapolis from controlling the line of scrimmage. If Tennessee allows the Colts to establish their rushing attack early, Ward could face additional pressure to produce points quickly. Indianapolis, meanwhile, will try to pressure Ward into difficult decisions and capitalize on turnovers. A Crucial AFC South Battle Sunday presents an important opportunity for both teams. Tennessee is searching for its first win, while Indianapolis needs a response after consecutive losses. The Titans will need a more productive offensive performance from Ward, while the Colts will look to Taylor and Jones to lead the way. With both teams eager to get back on track, execution and ball security could determine the outcome of this divisional matchup.

home.headline: Two Colts starters being evaluated for concussions after Wednesday's practice
home.blurb: Right guard Matt Goncalves and defensive end Jaylahn Tuimoloau were both listed as questionable due to concussion evaluations. The two players were also both listed as limited in practice and they were not wearing red non-contact jerseys during the portion of practice open to the media on Wednesday. Tuimoloau plays a defensive end position that has already been hit hard by injury. Veteran starter Arden Key is out due to a hamstring injury, and fellow free-agent pickup Micheal Clemons is on injured reserve due to a toe injury suffered in Kansas City. With those two out, Tuimoloau played a career-high 49 snaps in Pittsburgh on Sunday, only one fewer snap than fellow starter Laiatu Latu. Daniel Jones, the team’s starting quarterback, was listed as a full participant due to an ankle injury, the first time that designation has appeared this season. Indianapolis also listed slot receiver Josh Downs as limited due to both rest and a hamstring injury. INDIANAPOLIS — The Sunday status of two Colts starters appears to be in jeopardy after the release of the team’s Wednesday injury report. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. If either Goncalves or Tuimolaou are diagnosed with concussions, they will likely miss Sunday’s game against the Titans. Under the NFL’s concussion protocol, a player must complete five steps before returning to play, and there does not appear to be enough time to complete those five steps before Sunday. An injury to Tuimoloau would likely cause larger problems. Goncalves has been playing well at right guard, but the rest of the Colts offensive line is healthy, and Indianapolis has fourth-round pick Jalen Farmer waiting in the wings in case of injury. Rookies George Gumbs Jr. (11 snaps) and Caden Curry (9) were the only other defensive ends who played against the Steelers. Indianapolis signed veteran Carl Lawson to the practice squad last week, but he has not played. Tuimolaou and Goncalves are not the only concerns on Wednesday’s injury report. home.headline: Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts
home.blurb: The Colts are seeking consistency at linebacker, with snaps divided in Week 5 between Akeem Davis-Gaither (52 snaps), Austin Ajiake (32 snaps), CJ Allen (24 snaps) and Bryce Boettcher (11 snaps) with starting WILL linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) out. As with Davis-Gaither, the Colts see value in Pratt's experience not only in the NFL, but with Anarumo's system. Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts signed the 30-year-old Pratt, who started 12 games for them in 2025, to their practice squad on Tuesday. While Germaine Pratt went unsigned up until Tuesday, he found a way to still be involved in football. The 30-year-old veteran linebacker spent time in the summer as a volunteer coach at North Carolina State , where he worked with his alma mater's linebackers. He eventually had a tryout with the Dallas Cowboys, though he didn't sign. This week, Pratt got his chance to get back into playing instead of coaching. The Colts signed him to their practice squad on Tuesday, and while it's too early to tell if and when he'll make his 2026 debut, Pratt said his goal is to use his experience to bring leadership to the Colts' linebacker room. "Helping the defense, just being in this system for so long, that's all I know," Pratt said. "So help it stabilize and settle it down, make tackles, whatever the case may be, get some turnovers." Pratt has played all but four of his 112 NFL games for Lou Anarumo, his defensive coordinator with the Cincinnati Bengals (2019-2024) and Colts (2025). In 2025, Pratt signed with the Colts in October after being released by the Las Vegas Raiders and started 12 games, totaling 101 tackles, a forced fumble and an interception. The experienced WILL linebacker has had over 100 tackles with at least one interception and one forced fumble every year since 2023. "Just adding a veteran presence is big in there," head coach Shane Steichen said. "He's played a lot of football in this league, made a lot of plays, and any time you can add good players to your roster, you want to do that." In the immediate future, whether Pratt could factor into that group on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans – he'd have to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad – remains to be seen given he didn't participate in training camp and took the field for his first practice of the 2026 season on Wednesday. "I don't know the plan," Pratt said.
