The Dallas Cowboys entered Thursday night’s showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as 9.5-point favorites, yet they lost outright at home, destroying plenty of Survivor entries in the process. Week 5 had three teams that were obvious Survivor selections: Dallas, Houston and Cincinnati. They were all playing 0-4 teams, but only the Bengals and Texans came through. Luckily for the SI Betting team, neither of our editors selected the Cowboys this week, meaning that if you tailed our picks , you’re still alive heading into Week 6. Bye weeks are really starting to come into play in Survivor, as the Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings, Miami Dolphins and Bengals all won’t play in Week 6. One of the best strategies in Survivor this season has been fading the 0-5 Dolphins, so players will have to look elsewhere on Sunday. There are still some huge favorites in Week 6, the Los Angeles Rams are favored by double digits at home against the Arizona Cardinals, and the Kansas City Chiefs, Indianapolis Colts and New England Patriots are all favored by at least a touchdown at home. Each week, the SI Betting team of Iain MacMillan and Peter Dewey makes their favorite Survivor selections each week to help guide our readers through the season. Here’s a recap of our Week 5 selections before we dive into our favorite Survivor teams in Week 6. NFL Week 5 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Cincinnati Bengals (W) Iain MacMillan: Houston Texans (W) Both Dewey and MacMillan faded winless teams in Week 5, and both wins were relatively sweat free with the Texans blowing out Tennessee and Cincy cruising to a big lead in a seven-point win over Miami. There are still plenty of playoff contenders that we can choose from in Week 6, even in just a 14-game slate. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 6 Survivor Pool Picks Indianapolis Colts Indianapolis is going to be a popular pick in Survivor this week because it’s playing the Titans, but I’m willing to take a shot on Daniel Jones and company to get back to .500 at 3-3, especially at home. Indy is currently a seven-point favorite against the worst team in the AFC South. Cam Ward and the Titans have been downright awful on offense, ranking dead last in yards per play, 31st in EPA/Play and 26th in success rate during their 0-5 start. They’ve scored 20 or fewer points in every game, including three games where they scored 10 or less points. Indianapolis hasn’t done a great job of finishing drives this season, but it has one of the best kickers in the NFL in Spencer Shrader. So, Indy is able to get enough points on the board (like it did in Week 5) even if it doesn’t score a bunch of touchdowns. The Colts are allowing the third-most yards per play in the NFL on defense, which is a concern for them when it comes to this pick. However, Tennessee is 2-8 on the road in the Ward era, and it has covered the spread in just four of those games. The Indy offense isn’t a juggernaut, but it has moved the ball a lot better than the Titans, hanging 30 points on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2 while ranking 21st in success rate and 22nd in EPA/Play. I don’t see many spots where I’d willingly take the Colts in Survivor, so this is a way to use them and hopefully advance to Week 7. With more bye weeks ahead, it’s important to save a few top teams – if possible – for a game that may not be as much of a sure thing. Indy at home against the Titans is by far the most favorable game on the team’s schedule outside of a Nov. 15 home game against Miami. The Titans have been lost to open this season, and I don’t expect them to turn things around any time soon with how abysmal their offense has looked. The Colts may not cover, but they should handle business at home in Week 6. – Peter Dewey New England Patriots The New England Patriots proved last week that they still can show flashes of the team that won the AFC last season, especially when they play the weaker teams in the NFL. Their defense is a top 10 unit and Drake Maye can still torch a below average secondary. The Patriots now rank 10th in EPA per play, while the New York Jets rank 20th. New England is also 11th in opponent success rate, while New York is 23rd. That could all lead to big things for the Patriots in this divisional game. The Patriots have a ton of tough games on their schedule this season, including the Detroit Lions, Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos, so taking them when they're at home against either the Jets or Dolphins is going to be the move, which is why this is the week I'll take them at Gillette Stadium against Geno Smith and Aaron Glenn. Plus, New England is 18-2 at home in its last 20 games against the Jets. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. picks.blurb: Opening lines: Spread: Patriots -9.5 Moneyline: Patriots -440; Jets +340 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Patriots vs Jets expert picks Adam Kaufman: Patriots 28, Jets 17 That looked a little more like the Patriots we expected, didn't it? Drake Maye and the offense are finding their footing, and the Jets arrive after winning a game against the Browns that nobody needs to watch twice. New England's backfield takes a hit with TreVeyon Henderson expected to miss multiple weeks. More work for Rhamondre Stevenson, and another reason Maye needs to keep this passing game moving. Breece Hall's availability matters for New York. The Jets need sustained possessions, manageable third downs and a game that doesn't force them to chase points. I like the Patriots to control this one without needing another 45-point afternoon. Win the turnover battle and the rest should follow. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Patriots 31, Jets 17 In one of the sharpest early-season turnarounds we've seen thus far in 2026, Drake Maye is fully back to his NFL MVP runner-up form. That's a difficult blow for the Jets, who probably needed to face the more error-prone version of the quarterback in order to score an upset. Rookie David Bailey and the pass rush might give Gang Green a chance if they can keep Maye under pressure, but the defense's struggles to generate any takeaways cap the potential for chaos here. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Patriots 28, Jets 21 Everyone believes the Patriots are back. Are they? New England took advantage of a porous Bills defense and then an upstart Raiders bunch that had to travel across the country following a deflating defeat to the rival Chiefs. Credit the Patriots for taking care of business, but Drake Maye still has a long way to go before entering the circle of trust again. The Jets could get some reinforcements back this week and Aaron Glenn's defense has been respectable. The Patriots still get the job done, but it could be closer than some might expect. picks.headline: Patriots-Jets Week 6 preview: Keys to victory, prediction and more
picks.blurb: Patriots-Jets Week 6 preview: Keys to victory, prediction and more – NBC Sports Boston Celtics New England seeks its third straight win. By Justin Leger • Published October 15, 2026 • Updated on October 15, 2026 at 2:49 pm Nov 13, 2025; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (10) looks to pass the ball against the New York Jets in the first quarter at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images The New England Patriots snapped out of their early-season funk with back-to-back impressive wins over the Buffalo Bills and Las Vegas Raiders. Will they stay hot this Sunday against the New York Jets? If Drake Maye plays how he has over the last two weeks, the Jets won't stand much of a chance. The third-year quarterback is back to looking like his MVP-caliber self. He was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week after a 269-yard, three-TD performance vs. Buffalo, and should've earned the honor again after his 374-yard, five-TD gem against Vegas. The Patriots have dominated the Jets for the last two-and-a-half decades, but don't underestimate New York heading into this Week 6 matchup. Its pass defense has been among the NFL's best so far this season, so it won't be easy for Maye to keep his torrid stretch going, even if star wide receiver A.J. Brown is back in the mix. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels may have to lean more on the run game, which would mean a heavy workload for Rhamondre Stevenson with TreVeyon Henderson likely out with an ankle injury . As of Thursday, New England is a 7.5-point favorite to win Sunday's game at Gillette Stadium. What are the keys to matching those expectations? Here's our Pats-Jets Week 6 preview and prediction: Recent head-to-head matchups The Patriots beating up on the Jets is a tradition like no other. They've won 40 of their last 50 regular-season games against their storied AFC East rival since December 2001. They've lost to New York only twice in the last decade. Last season, the Patriots took care of business with a 13-point win at home before blowing the Jets out at MetLife Stadium. Here are the last three Patriots-Jets matchups: Week 11, 2025 at New England: 27-14 Patriots Week 17, 2025 at New York: 42-10 Patriots Week 8, 2024 at New England: 25-22 Patriots View this post on Instagram Key Stats David Bailey is a game-wrecker Jets edge rusher David Bailey could be a problem for the Patriots on Sunday. Bailey has five sacks through the first five weeks of his NFL career, including three in New York's 17-12 win over Cleveland last week. The undrafted rookie also racked up three tackles for loss and four total QB hits to earn the AFC Defensive Player of the Week honor. According to the NFL, Bailey became the first rookie since Jean Phillips with at least three sacks and three TFLs in the same game. David Bailey was a man on a mission in Week 5 🔥 @Pepsi https://t.co/DKOYWjlsLg Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel is well-aware of the challenge Bailey presents. "He's fast, explosive, instinctive," Vrabel said of Bailey on Wednesday. "He can bend, got a really good get off and is able to win at the top and corner. He uses his get off, so just like every week, we'll have to be very conscious of the front." Feed Rhamondre? The Jets have had one of the stingiest pass defenses this season, limiting opponents to an average of 175 passing yards per game (fourth-fewest in NFL). They could make it tough for Maye to push the ball downfield, giving McDaniels no choice but to lean on his running backs. That means we should expect a hefty workload for Rhamondre Stevenson. The Pats' RB2, TreVeyon Henderson, will miss time after suffering a high-ankle sprain last week. Stevenson and Corey Kiner are the only RBs currently on the active roster, though Lan Larison and Hassan Haskins are candidates to be elevated from the practice squad. While the Jets aren't terrible against the run, they're beatable. They rank 13th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (118). Patriots' key to victory Protect Drake Maye The Jets are tied for third in the NFL with 17 sacks this season. As mentioned above, rookie edge rusher David Bailey leads the group with five sacks, three coming last week vs. Cleveland. The Patriots offensive line will be tested against this menacing Jets front, especially if left tackle Will Campbell is out due to the knee injury he suffered last week. "I think they're physical. I think they have tenacity. I think they've got, I wouldn't say a new ferociousness, but you can see the difference on tape from last year," Maye said of the Jets defense on Wednesday. "They have some new faces, some new mentality. I think they're buying into how Coach [Aaron] Glenn wants to play defense, and I think you respect that. "You can see that on film. It pops out to you. They do a good job on the back end, mixing it up and also getting on you and grabbing you and playing physical. So, you can see that they're building something on defense, and it's really shown this year with how they played. Maye struggled mightily over the first three weeks of the season. Uncoincidentally, he was pressured often and sacked nine times in that span. Over his last two stellar games, Maye has only been sacked twice. Jets' key to victory Win the turnover battle The only way we see the Patriots losing to the Jets at home this week is if they fail to protect the football. That's how they earned both of their losses this season, with Maye tossing three interceptions in the season opener vs. Seattle and turning it over four times in Week 3 against Jacksonville. Fortunately for Maye and the Pats, the Jets don't pick anyone off. They went a record 21 games without an interception before safety Minkah Fitzpatrick finally snapped the streak in Week 4. That was New York's only INT so far this year. Fumbles are a different story. The Jets are tied for second in the NFL with five fumble recoveries this season. Maye has fumbled five times, Stevenson lost a fumble in Week 2, and Kiner coughed it up in last week's win. The Patriots must avoid giving the Jets extra possessions. If they do that, they should win this game pretty handily. Over the last two weeks, the Pats have resembled the 2025 team that finished 14-3 and represented the AFC in the Super Bowl. If they're even 75 percent as good as they were against Buffalo and Las Vegas, they should breeze past New York at home. That said, the Jets defense is capable of keeping this one close, especially if key Pats players are sidelined due to injuries. Running back TreVeyon Henderson and left tackle Will Campbell are expected to be out, and it remains to be seen whether star wideout A.J. Brown is ready to return from injured reserve. This could be a tougher matchup than many anticipate. But even if the Patriots are forced to embrace the "next man up" mentality yet again, a decent performance from Maye should be enough to propel them to 4-2. The New York Jets may need to abandon the volume of defensive pressure that helped them beat Cleveland when they visit the New England Patriots on Sunday. Locked On Jets host John Butchko pointed to New York’s blitz rate in Week 5 and argued that repeatedly sending extra rushers at Patriots quarterback Drake Maye would leave the Jets liable to big plays. (Butchko referred to the blitz rate as 47%, but TruMedia listed it as 52.3%.) Butchko said Maye’s mobility and success against pressure make this a different assignment from the rain-soaked matchup against the Browns. The Jets can still create a turnover by disguising pressure and picking their spots, but an overemphasis on the blitz would give Maye chances to extend plays and attack openings in the secondary. A more selective rush would put greater responsibility on the secondary to cover longer, especially if Brown is active. For a defense that has protected its red zone well, preventing a few vertical completions could matter more than chasing sacks. home.headline: Patriots week 6 injury report: AJ Brown returns, OTs banged up bad
home.blurb: "I mean, I think that we'll just focus on this week and see if guys are ready to go," Mike Vrabel said Wednesday about handling injuries ahead of this week and next week's Thursday Night Football game. "We obviously know we have a shortened week next week. It can’t impact our decisions to try to do everything we can to win this week. Then we’ll figure out where we are after that." The biggest story for the Patriots? The return of A.J. Brown, who missed Weeks 2 through 5 with a high-ankle sprain . He was designated to return off of IR this week, and will work to try and play this week against a Jets team he should thrive against. "He hasn't been out there, so I can't tell you until we actually see it," Vrabel said. "He hasn't been out there for four weeks, so we'll get him back out there practicing and see if he's ready to go in a couple days. And if not, then we have a 21-day window, and we'll go from there." Last week against the Raiders, the Patriots lost both TreVeyon Henderson and Will Campbell in a matter of minutes. Both players would leave the game and wouldn't return, and after tests on Monday, could end up missing some time . When reporters were present during Wednesday's practice, neither of them were spotted on the field with their teammates. Campbell did speak prior to going out to practice, but he only participated in a limited capacity. When Campbell was ruled out, the Patriots turned to first round rookie Caleb Lomu . He would play pretty good football from the left side — allowing just one pressure in 47 snaps. After starting the week as a limited participant, Christian Gonzalez was upgraded to a full participant for Thursday. He's been on the field working as a starter after missing the past two weeks of practice, and is now in line to make his return to the game field. Earlier this week, Gonzalez told reporters that he was "ready to go" for his battle with the Jets. Now that he's a full go in practice, the Patriots coaching staff is looking forward to seeing their top cornerback return to action. "He's the same guy," cornerbacks coach Justin Hamilton said. "He came back out and prepares, going to work, playing the game in his head like what he always has done." 3 Winners, 4 Losers of A.J. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. New England Patriots starting left tackle Will Campbell suffered a knee injury during this past Sunday's Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Campbell underwent MRI testing to determine the severity of his injury on Monday. And according to a report from NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the 22-year-old offensive lineman avoided a serious, long-term injury. Campbell is now considered "week-to-week" as the Patriots prepare for this coming Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the division-rival New York Jets. “We’ll see how the week goes,” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said of Campbell's injury status on Monday. “It’ll get looked at and continues to rehab. Wasn’t able to finish the game, so I don’t know how much time he’ll miss — if he’ll be back towards the end of the week, if he’ll be back Wednesday. We’ll take it day by day and see how he feels tomorrow, see what he does Wednesday, and keep you updated on the injury report.” After a slow start to the 2026 season, the Patriots are beginning to catch their stride. Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders marked the team's second consecutive victory and third win of the season thus far. Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Jets will kick off at 1 p.m. ET.

The Giants tied with the Washington Commanders in what ended up being one of the weirder games of the season. New York should have lost to Washington, so the fact that they tied is being taken as a win for the team. But the Giants know that they will need a better effort going forward this week as the team gets ready to face off against the New Orleans Saints at home. New Orleans will be coming into the game looking to stop the bleeding, with the Saints sitting with a record of 1-4 on the year. Both sides need a win this week for different reasons, and the Giants will try to remain perfect at home this season. New York can't overlook this Saints team despite their struggles this season; otherwise, the Giants could find themselves in a tight contest. Bleacher Report did game predictions for every contest this week, with Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford picking. In these predictions, every single expert went with the Giants to take down New Orleans. Much of this could be due to the Saints having their own problems this year, but the Giants have shown real promise as a team. Even with starting quarterback Jaxson Dart going down with an injury, the Giants have been able to stay the course. Backup signal-caller Jameis Winston has held down the fort well for New York, showing that he can get this team to the playoffs. But the problem with Winston is that he has been very inconsistent over the years in his career, and the Giants know this from the first few weeks of the season. As he gets ready to face off against New Orleans, Winston will need to make sure to stay focused. Winston can be very turnover-prone at times, and the Giants can't afford any issues against the Saints this week. The Giants defense has been a calling card for the team this season, helping them win a few games. And going against an explosive Saints passing attack, the New York secondary will need to be ready to go. New Orleans is looking to snap a three-game losing streak, while New York hopes to continue its strong start under first-year head coach John Harbaugh. The Saints enter the matchup at 1-4 after falling 23-13 to the Minnesota Vikings last week. The Giants are 3-1-1 after an exciting 27-27 overtime tie against the Washington Commanders. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Tyler Shough Leads the Saints New Orleans will rely on quarterback Tyler Shough to help get its offense back on track. The second-year quarterback has shown the ability to make plays through the air, but the Saints have struggled to find consistency during their recent losing streak. Through five games, Shough has thrown for 1,299 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions. He will need to make smart decisions and avoid turnovers against a Giants defense that has shown it can pressure opposing quarterbacks. Wide receiver Chris Olave remains one of New Orleans' most important offensive weapons. His ability to create separation and make plays downfield could be crucial as the Saints try to stretch the Giants' defense. Running back Alvin Kamara is another key player to watch. Establishing a productive rushing attack would help New Orleans create a more balanced offense and prevent New York from focusing primarily on Shough and the passing game. Head coach Kellen Moore needs his team to execute more consistently after the Saints managed just 142 total yards against Minnesota. Jameis Winston and the Giants Look to Build Momentum The Giants enter Sunday's game with confidence after rallying from a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit against Washington before settling for a tie. Quarterback Jameis Winston has stepped into the starting role and helped spark the offense. Against Washington, Winston led the Giants to 24 points on their four full drives in the third and fourth quarters, giving New York a chance to complete the comeback. The Giants also have playmakers capable of creating problems for New Orleans. Wide receiver Malik Nabers gives Winston a dangerous target, while tight end Isaiah Likely provides another option in the passing game. Harbaugh has emphasized his team's resilience, and the Giants will look to carry that mentality into their return home. A Key Matchup in the Trenches One of the biggest factors could be New York's pass rush against New Orleans' offensive line. If the Giants consistently pressure Shough, the Saints could struggle to sustain drives. New Orleans, meanwhile, needs its defense to contain Winston and prevent the Giants from producing the explosive plays that helped fuel their comeback last week. What to Watch Sunday The Saints need a complete performance to end their losing streak, while the Giants have an opportunity to strengthen their position in the NFC East. With Shough trying to steady New Orleans' offense and Winston leading a resilient Giants team, quarterback play and execution on third down could be decisive in this Week 6 matchup.

picks.headline: Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants
picks.blurb: Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers to advance to World Series TRENDING Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Lorenzo Styles Jr. #36 of the New Orleans Saints plays against the Minnesota Vikings during the first half of a game at Caesars Superdome on October 11, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Caleb Yaccarino Wed, October 14, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads I want to start this week's report by talking about this class. Like many, I have seen it ranked very low on lists of the best and worst classes from 2026. I don't disagree with those lists, and really, who can? Injuries, players being behind veterans, or some still needing to develop have kept this class from doing much, but you shouldn't lose faith in this group. The players who have been in the game have made plays that are good starting points, and although development matters, it's not like those players have been bad. Jordyn Tyson's injury is annoying to say the least, but hopefully we can forget about that once he's back. Do I think this class is going to be like 2025? No, but in hindsight, I think he could be a nice, middle-of-the-road draft class. Now onto the players: DT Christen Miller Finally, Christen Miller was able to get into the game on Sunday, and eventhough the Saints could not win, he did well in his short time. Miller made big plays against the run, took up blocks from offensive linemen to open up holes for other defensive linemen and the linebackers to stop the run, and in my opinion, proved he should be the starting nose tackle. It wasn't perfect, but it was enough for the Saints to play him more. This should hopefully be the case against the New York Giants, and to stop RB Cam Skattebo, you need a big defensive lineman that can prevent him from carrying the pile. TE Oscar Delp With the Vikings sending blitzes nearly every play, Delp had to step up as a blocker, and he did. The Giants are also at the top of the league in blitz rate, so Delp will be a primary blocker once again. I do hope the Saints utilize him as a receiver, because Noah Fant has had pre-snap issues this season, and prioritizing youth should be the plan moving forward. Try something new. OG Jeremiah Wright Speaking of trying something new, I wish Jeremiah Wright would get some snaps, but now that pressure is on the organization to win, a Cesar Ruiz trade feels less likely due to the risk. If a coaching change is made, I hope the next staff will give Wright a chance. WR Bryce Lance Last week, I said that it's clear Lance is not ready for WR3, and the Vikings game only reinforced that. The Saints need to make the move and put him at WR4 moving forward so he can learn. I know I have said to prioritize youth, but I also want to prioritize Tyler Shough's development, and Lance is negatively affecting that. WR Barion Brown Brown is a similar spot to Lance, but it's also clear he needs to figure out the return game as well. His fellow former LSU Tiger, Zavion Thomas, is in nearly the exact same spot with the Bears, but due to their offensive struggles with Caleb Williams being out, they have begun to utilize Thomas more. In addition, Thomas has improved as their main return man. Hopefully, the same can happen for Brown. RB CJ Donaldson Donaldson was thrown to the wolves trying to block the Vikings blitz, and although I felt he did a decent job, he did have a holding call on one of the plays. As a rusher, Donaldson did exactly what I thought, picking up tough yards that did help the Saints in their run game. Against the Giants, I want him to be included once again. OT Mason Murphy In probably the most confusing moment of the game, which is saying a lot, the Saints put in Mason Murphy on a random drive, then subbed him out for Asim Richards the next. At first, I thought Richards got injured, but Moore said after the game that it was planned. I actually thought Richards did better than usual, and Murphy wasn't great when he came in. I don't think the Saints will make this substitution again. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. Styles Jr. was back last game, which was nice to see, but his involvement was limited. I wouldn't be shocked if that changes after Jayden Price's release being cut, so Styles Jr. could be the return man next to Brown against the Giants. Injured players: WR Jordyn Tyson

picks.headline: Saints at Giants: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 6 game
picks.blurb: Opening lines: Spread: Giants -2.5 Moneyline: Giants -142; Saints +120 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Giants vs Saints expert picks Adam Kaufman: Giants 27, Saints 23 Jameis Winston against his former team? I love a good narrative, and you know there's going to be something worth watching here. The Giants keep giving themselves chances, and Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely should find room against a Saints defense that hasn't offered much resistance lately. New Orleans has dropped three straight, but New York's defense gives Tyler Shough a reasonable opportunity to bounce back from a dreadful showing versus Minnesota. This comes down to which quarterback turns more of those opportunities into touchdowns and fewer into a regrettable lowlight. Winston will probably make us nervous along the way. That's The Jameis Experience. I still like the Giants to finish the job at home. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Giants 21, Saints 17 The Giants' promising pass rush finally awakened against the Commanders. Rattling Tyler Shough could be the key to derailing a New Orleans attack that still doesn't offer much on the ground. Jameis Winston remains a volatile entity behind center, but his occasional highs give New York the chance to continue a fairly surprising start to the season given challenging circumstances. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Giants 24, Saints 17 It's time to pack up the Saints. You can point to injuries, Tyler Shough's poor play or a bad New Orleans defense. Take your pick. Whatever the reason, this unit is overmatched across the board and really has no business being a road favorite against anyone after five weeks. Say what you want about Jameis Winston, but he's slinging it for the G-Men and keeping his team afloat. The Giants will have every opportunity to capitalize on a bad NFC East and should have no trouble finding their fourth win of the season at home against the Saints. away.headline: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve
away.blurb: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve Welcome back, Zach Wood. The New Orleans Saints long snapper was a full participant at practice on Wednesday, marking his return from injured reserve. He'll need to continue practicing throughout the week in order to be activated for Sunday's game with the New York Giants , but all signs point to him snapping the ball at MetLife Stadium. The Saints released fill-in long snapper Cal Adomitis and don't have another player at the position on their roster. They also left a vacancy open and waiting for Wood on the 53-man roster once he gets the green light. Wood, 33, won the job back in 2017 and was the long snapper for New Orleans in 150 consecutive regular season games (plus seven playoff games), finally ending his streak when a calf strain forced him out of action the last four weeks. The fear was that he would have needed even more time to recover, but he's ahead of schedule and expected to be back in the lineup. Wood has made quite a career for himself as a former rookie free agent out of SMU. He actually spent some time with the Dallas Cowboys when Kellen Moore was the backup quarterback in 2016 and part of the 2017 preseason. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve Brewers sweep Dodgers to advance to World Series John Sigler, Saints Wire Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:56 AM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads He's been missed. Adomitis had some hiccups and drew an untimely penalty during Week 5's loss to the Minnesota Vikings , so getting Wood back on the field should help steady the operation. You just hope he isn't rushing himself back too soon.

home.headline: Giants star Malik Nabers’ honest take on knee injury return should scare rest of NFL
home.blurb: “I still got like 20% left to get to. 30%. 20 to 30%. But yeah, I mean, I got a lot more left. I got a lot more ahead of me than I see in my potential,” Nabers said. “Even though those two big games that I had, I left many plays out there. Like, just probably drops, dropped the ball on that screen that could have went for 60. That game could have looked a whole lot different, or just the back of the end zone, just focusing on the ball, or just anything plays, or just diving for the ball.” “That I feel like I could have catched. Like I’m never a person that’s gonna always come back and be like I could have got a better ball. I just always feel like I can catch it. Just got to put my body in a position for me to make that catch. So I just feel like I left a lot of plays out there, and that could have been a whole different ball game.” Malik Nabers will look forward to helping the Giants return to the playoffs. In Year 1 under head coach John Harbaugh, they are off to a solid start despite suffering injuries to key players. Malik Nabers showed his goals of determination of getting back to superstar form that will surely excite New York Giants fans for the rest of the 2026 season and beyond. Nabers is going through the third season of his NFL career with the Giants. He is coming off injury rehab after tearing his ACL last year. Nabers talked about his performances so far this season with media, per reporter Jordan Raanan. He revealed he is getting closer to his form before the ACL injury, expressing confidence that he’s only getting better. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. And few teams are more disappointing thus far than the Philadelphia Eagles . Might Nick Sirianni get a pink slip if his club loses at home Sunday against a rested and surging Carolina Panthers team? The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. It's not just his clock management, but his offense has been lousy during this skid in averaging 14.7 points and 217 yards per game while converting just 22.2% of third downs. The PPG is the fewest for Philly through five games since 2012, and the YPG the fewest through five since 1999. A juggled offensive line hasn't helped. With Lane Johnson having retired, Cam Jurgens traded and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, the team has replaced three starters already. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The Eagles are averaging a scant 3.5 yards per play with both off the field this season, compared to 5.3 in all other situations. It's possible the Eagles are down to their No. 4 tailback because No. 2 Tank Bigsby is on IR and No. 3 Will Shipley was hurt against the Jags. This will mark the first time the Eagles will take the field sitting below .500 since 2021, when they were 6-7. The 76 straight games played without a losing record was the longest streak in team history. The overall NFL record is 145 by the Patriots from 2003-12. Carolina comes off its bye with its 2-2 mark the team's best four-game start since 2021. It's also good enough for the lead in the ultra-weak NFC South – the Panthers are +130 favorites. We get a former all-Alabama quarterback matchup here in Bryce Young vs. Hurts with Young off to his best start and perhaps answering all those lingering questions that have dogged the former No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to Young and sensational second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan , the Panthers rank top five in the league in scoring offense (30.3 PPG), total offense (405.8 YPG) and passing offense (301.3 YPG). The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Young also led the NFL entering his bye week with 11 completions on deep throws (20+ air yards). He is 0-1 against Hurts in the NFL as the Eagles beat the visiting Panthers 22-16 in the most recent meeting in December 2024. The dual-threat quarterback hasn't been at his best this season, but he gives Philly's offense a different dimension in the ground game that McKee can't really replicate. The Philadelphia Eagles made the long trek back from London after a mindboggling, crushing defeat where victory was essentially secured. The Panthers have the advantage this week, it seems. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. "The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. "The Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. Carolina enters the game at 2-2 following a bye week, while Philadelphia sits at 2-3 after suffering three consecutive losses. The Eagles are coming off a heartbreaking 17-16 defeat against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, where a late field goal sealed another frustrating result. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET at Lincoln Financial Field, with the game airing on CBS. Bryce Young Leads Carolina's Offense Panthers quarterback Bryce Young will be one of the biggest players to watch Sunday. Young has shown significant improvement during the 2026 season, helping Carolina develop a more productive passing attack. His connection with rookie wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan has become an important part of the offense, giving the Panthers a dangerous combination through the air. Carolina's offense looked particularly effective in its victory over the Detroit Lions before the bye week. Young will look to carry that momentum into Philadelphia against an Eagles defense that has struggled to consistently close out games. Head coach Dave Canales will also want to establish the running game and keep Young in manageable situations. If Carolina can maintain balance offensively, it could create opportunities to attack Philadelphia downfield. Tanner McKee Takes Over for Philadelphia Philadelphia faces a significant challenge at quarterback after Jalen Hurts was ruled out because of a superficial blood clot in his leg. Backup Tanner McKee is expected to start in his place. McKee has limited NFL starting experience, making Sunday's matchup an important opportunity for him to demonstrate what he can do against Carolina's defense. Head coach Nick Sirianni will need to put McKee in favorable situations while finding ways to generate offense despite the team's recent struggles. Philadelphia's offensive line has also undergone significant changes, and the Eagles have struggled to establish their usual rushing attack. Getting the running game going could help take pressure off McKee and allow the offense to find a rhythm. An Important NFC Matchup For Carolina, Sunday's game represents an opportunity to take advantage of an Eagles team dealing with several challenges and return from the bye with a statement victory. Philadelphia desperately needs to stop its losing streak and regain confidence at home. With Young leading Carolina's offense and McKee stepping into a starting role for the Eagles, execution and turnovers could play major roles in determining the outcome. Both teams have plenty to prove, making Sunday's matchup an important test for their respective seasons.

away.blurb: Quarterback Jalen Hurts is the latest player to go down, as he's been diagnosed with a superficial blood clot and will not play in Week 6 against the Carolina Panthers. away.headline: NFL analyst picks Panthers over Eagles for Week 6 matchup
away.blurb: Besides being out of running backs, the other problem for the Eagles is that they've struggled to stop the pass this year and they're facing a Panthers team that is SECOND in the NFL in passing yards per game. I never thought in my entire life that I'd type out anything like that about Carolina's offense, but here we are. The deck is stacked against the Eagles, so I have no choice here; I'm taking the Panthers. PICK: Panthers (+1.5) 27-24 over Eagles However, the Eagles are far from healthy going into Sunday's matchup with the Panthers. Their offensive line is battered by injuries, their right tackle Lane Johnson just suddenly retired and they're down to their practice-squad running backs. Carolina has plenty of injury issues of their own , but at least one analyst thinks they can pull off a win this week. John Breech at CBS Sports is predicting a victory for the Panthers: It's not a wild take given the situation. In fact, they were one Xavier Legette drop away from upsetting the Eagles the last time they visited Philly two years ago. Plus, the Eagles' struggling offense may not be able to take advantage of what might be the Panthers' biggest weakness—their banged-up cornerback room. Even without starters Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, Carolina might not have too difficult of a time keeping down the league's fifth-worst passing attack—especially if it's still missing their top wideout in DeVonta Smith. home.headline: Jalen Hurts Injury Update Causes Massive Shift in Panthers vs. Eagles Odds for NFL Week 6
home.blurb: Quarterback Jalen Hurts is the latest player to go down, as he's been diagnosed with a superficial blood clot and will not play in Week 6 against the Carolina Panthers. Hurts apparently played with the clot in his calf on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, but the team decided to rule him out for this week after an ultra sound revaled movement in the clot. Jalen Hurts Injury Update Causes Massive Shift in Panthers vs. Eagles Odds for NFL Week 6 Skip to main content ON SI The Philadelphia Eagles can't avoid the injury bug. Losing Hurts has impacted the Eagles' odds for Week 6 against the Panthers, as they are now home underdogs of more than a field goal. The Eagles opened as 1.5-point favorites at home in this game, even with Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and others dealing with injuries. However, Hurts' absence caused this line to flip completely, as the Panthers are now 3.5-point favorites on the road in the odds at DraftKings . Tanner McKee is in line to start for the Eagles in Week 6, and that's a clear downgrade to the team's offense. McKee completed just 21 of his 40 pass attempts in his lone start in 2025, throwing one score and pick in a loss to the Washington Commanders. This season, Hurts has completed 57.8 percent of his passes for 933 yards, eight scores and three picks. He's also added 107 rushing yards and a score on the ground. The dual-threat quarterback hasn't been at his best this season, but he gives Philly's offense a different dimension in the ground game that McKee can't really replicate. At 2-3, the Eagles are already second in the odds to win the NFC East and have seen their Super Bowl odds fall in the last few weeks. If Hurts missed extended time, Philly's playoff odds are going to take a hit as well. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. picks.headline: Steelers vs. Buccaneers Preview: Pittsburgh Travels to Tampa for Crucial Week 6 Matchup
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Buccaneers Preview: Pittsburgh Travels to Tampa for Crucial Week 6 Matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers to advance to World Series TRENDING Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Photo by: Charles LeClaire Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 8:10 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers travel to Florida on Sunday to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in an important Week 6 matchup between two teams looking to build momentum. Pittsburgh enters the game at 3-2, while Tampa Bay is 1-4 after finally earning its first victory of the season. The Buccaneers are coming off an impressive 24-16 road win over the Dallas Cowboys, while the Steelers are looking to get back on track in a competitive AFC North race. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET at Raymond James Stadium, with the game airing on CBS. Aaron Rodgers Leads Pittsburgh's Offense Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers remains one of the biggest storylines heading into Sunday's matchup. The veteran quarterback is playing his 18th NFL season and brings plenty of experience to a Pittsburgh offense that has shown flashes of success. Rodgers' ability to read defenses, make adjustments at the line of scrimmage and deliver accurate passes will be important against a Tampa Bay defense looking to build on its performance against Dallas. Head coach Mike Tomlin will want his offense to establish consistency early. Pittsburgh has alternated wins and losses through its first five games, making Sunday's contest an opportunity to gain momentum before the season progresses further. The Steelers will also look to take advantage of their defensive talent, particularly their ability to pressure opposing quarterbacks and disrupt offensive rhythm. Jalon Daniels Looks to Continue Tampa Bay's Turnaround Tampa Bay will likely turn to rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels , who has stepped into a starting role while Baker Mayfield deals with a thumb injury. Daniels helped lead the Buccaneers to their first win of the season against Dallas, and the team will hope he can build on that performance against Pittsburgh. Head coach Todd Bowles has emphasized physical football, and Tampa Bay's running game was a major factor in its victory over the Cowboys. The Buccaneers rushed for more than 240 yards and forced three turnovers, providing a formula they will look to repeat Sunday. However, facing Pittsburgh's defense presents a different challenge. Daniels will need to protect the football and avoid putting the Buccaneers in difficult situations. Key Matchups to Watch The battle in the trenches could determine how this game unfolds. Pittsburgh will look to pressure Daniels, while Tampa Bay must find ways to protect its young quarterback and maintain its productive rushing attack. The Steelers also need to contain Tampa Bay's playmakers and avoid allowing explosive runs to change the game's momentum. An Important Test for Both Teams Sunday's matchup gives Pittsburgh an opportunity to improve its road performance and strengthen its position in the AFC North. Tampa Bay, meanwhile, will try to turn its victory over Dallas into its first winning streak of the season. With Rodgers' experience facing Daniels' opportunity to establish himself, the quarterback matchup adds another layer of intrigue to Sunday's contest.

picks.headline: Buccaneers, Steelers: Week 6 game preview
picks.blurb: Buccaneers, Steelers: Week 6 game preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers to advance to World Series TRENDING Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Buccaneers, Steelers: Week 6 game preview Aug 16, 2025; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving (7) catches a touchdown pass in front of Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Payton Wilson (41) during the first quarter at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Will Walsh Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Week 6 is set to be rolling into living rooms all throughout the nation and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are no longer winless. Todd Bowles and his pewter pirates managed to pull out a sensationally shocking upset of the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football. Behind the mighty galloping of Bucky Irving and the poise of UDFA Jalen Daniels, Tampa's marauders took over AT&T Stadium. This Sunday (for the third week in a row), it'll be another classic blueblood NFL franchise on the schedule for the Buccaneers— The Pittsburgh Steelers. "The offense can't score if they don't have the ball." How can the Buccaneers win? ARLINGTON, TX - OCTOBER 08: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on October 8, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bucs need to make sure they stay on schedule and stick to their gameplan. There are NFL teams that have the benefit of being able to get into different types of games and win in a variety of ways— The Buccaneers are not that team. If a win is in the cards, they need to make sure they are playing the hand that best suits them. Last week, in Dallas, Tampa did a phenomenal job of staying in the realm of football that they themselves are comfortable playing. The Buccaneers kept the ball on the ground, dominated time of possession— Starting with a 10-minute opening drive, and kept Dallas off-kilter. That dictation was not only an advantage for Tampa Bay, it's the reason they won. That in turn made the Cowboys play the game the Buccaneers needed to play, not the one Dallas wanted to play. It would be easy to say, 'If Bucky Irving rushes for nearly 200 yards, the Buccaneers have a good chance of winning' , but it's more than the yards on the stat sheet. Irving's performance was eye-popping, but it was the offense's ability to stay on the field that won Tampa Bay the game. The Buccaneers finished the game with just shy of 40 minutes time of possession, while Dallas' heralded offense held the ball for just 20. That discrepancy is catastrophic for any team to be on the wrong side of— Personified through the consistent cutaways by Amazon's broadcast as they kept showing defeated, disengaged, and dispirited Dallas Cowboys on the sideline. Consecutive weeks with 40 minutes of possession may not be on the docket, however, will the Buccaneers' offense be able to keep themselves steady, avoid turnovers, and push Pittsburgh to play the type of game Tampa wants to play? "The question isn't who is going to let me; it's who is going to stop me." How can the Buccaneers lose? The Steelers have had some inconsistent offense this year, but they've had 24-plus points in each of the last three weeks (30, 24, 34). Of course, they can't score if they don't play (See the above portion of this article). The Buccaneers' second best option for keeping Pittsburgh's points down, besides pilfering clock, is turnovers. Tampa's turnover differential on the season is not glamourous (-2). Maybe even more absurd, that hideous -2 sits boldly after the Bucs just had a +3 in their last contest. Aside from points themselves, nothing has ever been, or will ever be, a more clear determinant of wins and losses than turnovers. Teams that take the ball away win a lot more than teams that lose the ball. Having the ball means having more chances to score, more chances to score means more better odds you will score; ergo, turnovers are good. More importantly, for a struggling, very one-dimensional team like the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, turnovers level the playing field. The scenario is two-fold. Not only does it fall on your defense to force them, but your offense must avoid turnovers like a coach on the hot seat must avoid losing. Last week, Tampa hit the trifecta— Their defense (and special teams) took the ball away from Dallas three times. Jalen Daniels and the Bucs' offense did not turn the ball over at all and their coach on the heat seat avoided a loss. This week, it's not Dak Prescott it's Aaron Rodgers. Aaron Rodgers is a historically anti-turnover prone quarterback. The former Packers' legend, Jets' bust, and current Steelers' stopgap, has quite literally the greatest touchdown to interception ratio in NFL history— As in, number one. Rodgers is not the type of quarterback that you want to face if the gameplan is get the ball— however , against all odds, Tampa Bay's ever assailed head coach Todd Bowles has actually had a healthy level of success against Rodgers during his Bucs' tenure. The two haven't matched up since Rodgers left Green Bay, but the duels have actually largely favored Bowles. In three games versus Todd Bowles' Tampa Bay defense, Rodgers has a losing record and has looked extremely ordinary. The four-time NFL MVP has wracked up just five touchdowns and he's also tossed four interceptions. The backdrop is laid out much differently for the 2026 edition, Rodgers has a new team, a new (his old) coach, is playing at a completely different level (which may actually further favor Bowles), and Bowles does not have nearly the same defensive firepower he once did. Sunday, will likely be the last time the two battle— A final chapter in the story. The storylines for Sunday's Bowles-Rodgers epilogue, can Todd Bowles get him again? Rodgers has yet to play a clean game against Bowles' Bucs. Will the Buccaneers' offense be able to stay mistake free for a second straight week? Turnovers, like they had against Rodgers' former team two weeks ago, will almost assuredly sink them into a self-dug 1-5 hole.

away.headline: Rico Dowdle goes full, but Steelers aren’t taking the ball from Jaylen Warren
away.blurb: Rico Dowdle practiced fully on Thursday, and Mike McCarthy made one thing clear: Jaylen Warren remains the Pittsburgh Steelers’ featured back. Dowdle has missed three games with a toe injury. In that stretch, Warren gave Pittsburgh every reason to rethink its backfield plan . More depth? Absolutely. A return to equal workloads? Warren hasn’t given them a reason for that. The official October 15 injury report moved Dowdle from limited to full participation. Keeanu Benton (ankle) and Jalen Ramsey (wrist) returned to limited work after sitting Wednesday. Jamel Dean (ankle) and DeShon Elliott (knee) remained limited. T.J. Watt and Cameron Heyward practiced fully after rest entries the day before. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) missed practice again, and McCarthy has already said both receivers will miss Sunday’s game at Tampa Bay. Dowdle’s full practice gives the Steelers a better shot at having him available. It doesn’t put him in Sunday’s lineup (yet) or assign him half of Warren’s carries. McCarthy said Warren’s role won’t change. I’d hold him to that. Pittsburgh can use Dowdle without interrupting what its best offensive player has been doing. Give Dowdle a chance to spell Warren if he’s active. With Wilson and Skowronek out and Michael Pittman Jr. on injured reserve, Pittsburgh may continue to lean heavily on Warren as both a runner and a receiving outlet. Another back could keep him fresh through a full game. The defense got news it needed, too. Wednesday’s report kept Benton and Ramsey out of practice ; both made it back Thursday. Benton’s progress is huge because Derrick Harmon’s injured-reserve stint already put more on Pittsburgh’s interior line. Benton’s limited work helps, though Heyward and the other tackles still need to be ready if his ankle restricts him. Ramsey’s return gives Patrick Graham a better chance to keep his options at corner, slot, and safety. Dean’s second limited practice is another useful step after he missed the Colts game. Elliott could help at safety, but he remains on injured reserve and needs a roster activation before he can play. None of those practice labels settle Sunday’s lineup. Pittsburgh Steelers have room for Rico Dowdle without an even Jaylen Warren-split But Dowdle doesn't need a fixed share of touches before he plays a snap after his toe injury. He hasn't played since Atlanta. The offensive line is playing far better than it was in Week 2, which could be a welcome sight for a player who produced just 37 yards on 15 carries. At receiver, offensive coordinator Brian Angelichio discussed deploying Pat Freiermuth, Darnell Washington, and Robert Tonyan in different tight end packages. That gives Aaron Rodgers ways to work around the shortage while Pittsburgh decides whether to elevate practice squad receiver Brandon Smith. away.headline: Steelers Week 6 Thursday Injury Report: Latest Updates and Analysis
away.blurb: Both teams have plenty to gain from Sunday’s matchup, as each remains within reach of its division leader. The Steelers sit one game behind the Baltimore Ravens , while the Buccaneers trail the Carolina Panthers by 1.5 games. Tampa Bay is preparing to start rookie Jalon Daniels again, although Baker Mayfield could return. Meanwhile, Pittsburgh hopes to get at least one of its two starting defensive backs back this week. The Pittsburgh Steelers received several encouraging injury updates Thursday ahead of their Week 6 matchup against the Buccaneers. Running back Dowdle and defensive tackle Heyward progressed to full participation, while Watt also practiced fully after resting Wednesday. Benton improved from a DNP to a limited participant, and Ramsey returned to practice on a limited basis after missing Wednesday’s session with a wrist injury. However, Pittsburgh still has concerns at wide receiver and in the secondary. Wilson and Skowronek missed their second consecutive practices, putting their availability in question, while Elliott and Dean remained limited. Elliott is eligible to return from injured reserve, but must show he is 100% ready to return. Friday’s practice will be critical for determining whether those players can return to action, particularly with the Steelers needing as much healthy depth as possible heading into Sunday’s game. The Pittsburgh Steelers are headed to Raymond James Stadium, where they won Super Bowl XLIII, to take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6 . Pittsburgh enters the matchup at 3-2 against a 1-4 Tampa Bay team, but don’t let the Buccaneers’ record fool you. All five of their games have been decided by one possession, and they just pulled off a major upset on the road against the Dallas Cowboys with a rookie quarterback. Arizona is 1-4 and coming off a disappointing 45-21 defeat against the Detroit Lions. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. Matthew Stafford Leads the Rams Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford will be a major factor in Sunday's game as Los Angeles looks to rebound from its difficult loss to Buffalo. Stafford has thrown for 1,572 yards and nine touchdowns through five games, establishing himself as the centerpiece of an offense capable of producing explosive plays. However, six interceptions have created problems, and protecting the football will be important against Arizona. Head coach Sean McVay will look to get the offense back on track by utilizing his talented group of playmakers. Williams has recorded 343 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns, making him an important part of Los Angeles' offensive attack. The Rams will also need to adjust along the offensive line, with left tackle Alaric Jackson suspended for Sunday's matchup. Brissett has thrown for 1,110 yards and nine touchdowns this season. Despite Arizona's struggles, he has shown the ability to move the football through the air and keep the offense competitive. Tight end Trey McBride remains one of his most reliable targets, entering the matchup with 42 receptions for 308 yards and three touchdowns. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love has also contributed to Arizona's offense, although his availability and workload will be worth monitoring after he missed practice Wednesday with an ankle issue. Arizona needs a stronger defensive performance after allowing 45 points against Detroit. With Stafford leading an explosive passing attack and Brissett looking to keep the Cardinals competitive, both quarterbacks will face important challenges. The Rams and Cardinals have plenty to prove, and Sunday's matchup could be an important moment for both teams as the NFC West race continues.

away.headline: Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams
away.blurb: TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up. Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. "And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday." Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air. "I think early at his career [he battled injuries], but you had the right [ankle] early, and then now you got the left one. So now you're just kind of — it's just double dipping. The right side, the preseason one's fine. It's the other one right now that's the lingering issue. They're ankles, you know, it's an ankle. I'm not a doctor, and each body's a little bit different," LaFleur continued. "Like the way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable, like he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened kind of when the regular season started, and it just lingered." Has Love lost any of his explosiveness? "You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur added. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So I mean I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again the the rest for him is going to be vital." home.headline: Rams Move Closer to Getting Keagen Trost Back Following Alaric Jackson Suspension
home.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams have officially opened rookie offensive lineman Keagen Trost’s practice window ahead of Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals. If all goes well, the plan is to activate Trost from injured reserve and have him available against Arizona. Head coach Sean McVay noted on Tuesday that the plan would be for David Quessenberry to start in Jackson’s place. However, given the lack of depth at tackle, McVay also said that the team would look into opening Trost’s practice window with the expectation that he would be available against the Cardinals. “‘DQ’ will take that spot. Then that'll also open up the opportunity for us to start Trost’s clock with the expectation of him being back out there this week,” said McVay on Tuesday. McVay added on Thursday that as long as Trost is feeling good, the Rams expect him to be available for Sunday’s game. The team will also be mindful of not putting him in a situation that isn’t good for his development, given how long it’s been since Trost played. The Rams drafted Trost in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Trost had a good summer, playing with the first- and second-team offenses at multiple positions. During the first preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs, Trost hurt his hamstring. Prior to roster cutdowns, the Rams put Trost on injured reserve to keep another roster spot available. “It’s not too big for him. He’s a very mature rookie,” said McVay last week on the Coach McVay show . “Got the ability to play on both the left and right side. Probably a little bit more comfortable on the right, but certainly you see the athleticism, the flexibility to get in and out of right- and-left handed stances. I like what he’s about and think he’s got a bright future for us.” While Justin Dedich remains on injured reserve, it makes sense that the Rams are prioritizing Trost given the need at tackle. Dedich can only play on the interior, while Trost is more of a tackle who can move inside. If the Rams were to need depth on the interior, Dedich would be an option.For now, the Rams are moving toward activating Trost from injured reserve. The Rams haven’t gotten much production out of their rookie class this season. While Trost will likely serve as Quessenberry’s backup on Sunday, his return will provide much-needed depth at tackle. On Tuesday, the NFL announced that Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson would be suspended for the next two games . Jackson was caught on camera throwing a punch at Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb following Monday night’s loss. After an appeal, Jackson’s suspension was reduced to just one game. During training camp, the Rams seemed pleased with Trost. While he’s more comfortable on the right side, McVay has talked about his ability to play on the left if needed. Trost can also slide in at guard.
