picks.blurb: Chiefs-Chargers betting line & game prediction: KC faces desperate AFC West rival - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers to advance to World Series TRENDING Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III (9) dives to the pylon to complete a 22-yard touchdown scamper against the Las Vegas Raiders during a Week 4 NFL game at Allegiant Stadium in Paradise, Nevada, on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. (David Brytus/IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Pete Sweeney Thu, October 15, 2026 at 12:30 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs return from their bye week hoping to build on their perfect 4-0 record as they welcome a Los Angeles Chargers team that has lost five straight to start the season. Sunday's game marks the second straight AFC West matchup for the Chiefs and Chargers. Kansas City defeated the Las Vegas Raiders 30-27 on the road in Week 4, and this past Sunday, Los Angeles lost 23-17 to the Denver Broncos. How to watch Chargers at Chiefs Kickoff: 3:25 p.m. Central Time Where: Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -8.5 Behind the LAC-KC matchup The last time the Chargers visited Arrowhead Stadium, it was one of the grimmest days in a decade for the dynastic Chiefs. In a game in which Kansas City needed a win to keep its playoff hopes alive, Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL and LCL , with Los Angeles eventually winning 16-13. The Chargers beat the Dallas Cowboys the following week but dropped two games to close the season, missing the playoffs. The December victory against Dallas still stands as their last win here in mid-October. As expected, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid is not looking too much into their winless start. "Good football team — we know that," Reid said. "Records don't matter. They've been in every game, and they're playing their tail off. So we're going to get ready for a tough AFC West battle there. Jim (Harbaugh) does a heck of a job with that crew." To Reid's point — and it's been a rather familiar one in Kansas City — the Chargers have lost each of their last three games by one score. Reid would later note Los Angeles' long injury list, which will have an impact on both sides of the ball. Because of several injuries to their offensive line, including those to star tackles Rashawn Slater (ankle) and Joe Alt (neck), the Chargers used a rookie-heavy group against Denver, with Herbert taking five sacks. Slater is currently on injured reserve, and Alt did not practice Wednesday. Through five games, Herbert has taken 17 total sacks — the second-highest mark in the league. The stat could play well for the Chiefs, who are looking for their first sack since recording four in their opening-night win against the Broncos. "There's a lot of things that go into it," defensive end George Karlaftis said. "From protection and quarterback getting rid of the ball and all that kind of stuff. Ultimately, for us as a front seven, defensive line, we've got to get the quarterback on the ground by any means necessary, and we've got to do a better job of that." Los Angeles' woes aren't exclusive to the offensive line. In addition to Alt, the Chargers listed 19 more players on their Wednesday injury report. Left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), wide receiver Tre Harris (hamstring), cornerback Donte Jackson (hamstring) and safety Derwin James (hamstring) were among those held out because of injury. James has missed the last two games, and if he misses a third, it could spell trouble against tight end Travis Kelce. Now in his 14th season, Kelce has had his share of battles with James, and he comes into the game leading the Chiefs with 246 receiving yards. Kelce's involvement will be even more important with Tyquan Thornton heading to injured reserve and Rashee Rice missing the first practice of the week because of his hamstring injury. The injuries to Thornton and Rice should mean additional opportunities for Jalen Royals, Cyrus Allen and the recently reacquired Justin Watson, who may be elevated from the practice squad. "They've put in the work," quarterback Patrick Mahomes said. "We've had the guys in front of them with Tyquan going out there and playing great football, and so they've had to put in the work at practice. And they've been doing that and doing that. And so now their number gets called, and they're gonna step into the role and do their job. And so I'm excited for them." Of course, the Chiefs' 2026 offensive plan begins with running back Kenneth Walker, who will look to pick up right where he left off following his extraordinary start . Entering Week 6, Walker ranks among the league's top-five players with 621 yards from scrimmage, and Pro Football Focus credits him with a league-leading 39 missed tackles forced. Walker's seamless impact should help keep Mahomes upright, with the Los Angeles edge group of Khalil Mack, Akheem Mesidor and Tuli Tuipulotu having combined for 6.5 sacks. The presence of Walker has opened up play-action shots that are working well for the Chiefs. Although left tackle Josh Simmons (back) practiced on a limited basis Wednesday , Reid said the Chiefs plan to ease him back in, which means his highly anticipated return may have to wait until next week at the earliest. The Chargers hired offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel this offseason with hopes of getting the most out of Herbert, but offensive-line injuries and other struggles have contributed to a difficult start for the quarterback, who has thrown seven interceptions and posted a 70.2 passer rating. Herbert has often responded to the pocket collapsing by using his legs, as he's rushed for 142 yards on 24 attempts, or 5.9 yards a carry. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo will be tasked with pushing Herbert toward what Harbaugh has called "desperation time," where Herbert has tried to carry the entire offense himself. That could mean a Chiefs-friendly script that presents Kansas City's healthy secondary with turnover opportunities. With all the injuries to the passing offense, Los Angeles may need to muck up the game and rely heavily on its three-headed rushing attack of Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. No matter how they make it happen, the Chargers will have to find a way to win or risk entering their Week 8 bye without a victory. Chargers-Chiefs game prediction If not for the Chargers' outrageous injury list, this would make for the perfect situation to pick a surprise Los Angeles win, or at the very least a cover. But when you examine everything — the Chiefs' hot start, the reinvigorated offense led by Walker and Reid's impressive career record coming off a bye — it all seems like too much. The Chargers initially make it interesting before the Chiefs settle in and continue doing what they have done all season. Winner: Chiefs 31, Chargers 19 | Cover: Chiefs Sweeney's record: (4-0-0) | Against the spread: (2-2-0)

Kansas City is 4-0 after its bye, while Los Angeles is 0-5 following a 23-17 loss to Denver. Kickoff at Arrowhead Stadium is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. The Chiefs are favored by 8.5 points, but a routine favorite winning comfortably would hardly qualify as a bold prediction. Instead, this forecast projects an exceptional rushing performance, an unexpected Chargers defensive highlight and a fourth-quarter rally that changes the complexion of the afternoon without changing the winner. Kenneth Walker III rushes for 200 yards and three touchdowns Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Walker has already accumulated 537 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 87 carries through four games. That translates to more than six yards per attempt, giving Kansas City a foundation for dominating without asking Patrick Mahomes to carry every possession. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Chiefs average 6.5 yards per offensive play compared with the Chargers' 4.8. Their third-down conversion rate is also substantially better: 44% against 34.85%. Those advantages can sustain drives and produce the repeated rushing opportunities necessary for a monster individual afternoon. The prediction goes beyond another efficient outing. Walker reaches 200 rushing yards for the game and scores three times, becoming the central reason Kansas City controls possession and repeatedly finishes drives. There is an important limitation: Los Angeles allows only 5.0 yards per play, the same figure as Kansas City. This is not a forecast built on pretending the Chargers cannot defend. It depends on Walker maintaining his explosiveness while the Chiefs create an unusually favorable game script. If Kansas City builds an early advantage, sustained rushing volume can turn Walker's strong start into the biggest performance of his season. The Chargers intercept Patrick Mahomes twice, including a pick-six Mahomes has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions through four games, with a 106.2 passer rating. Predicting two interceptions in one afternoon means Los Angeles matches his entire season total, despite entering winless. The statistical route to that surprise exists. The Chargers allow opponents to convert just 31.25% of third downs, compared with Kansas City's 37.04%. Forcing longer, obvious passing situations could provide opportunities that disappear when Walker keeps the offense ahead of schedule. Los Angeles needs more than ordinary defensive stops because its offense averages just 16.8 points per game. A defensive touchdown would change both field position and scoreboard pressure without requiring Justin Herbert to repeatedly rescue stalled possessions. The call is that one aggressive coverage read becomes an interception return for a touchdown, while another takeaway interrupts a promising Chiefs drive. That would be an unexpected blemish on Mahomes' efficient opening month. It would also illustrate why a team's record does not eliminate its capacity to produce a game-changing individual moment. Justin Herbert leads a 17-point fourth quarter, but Kansas City survives Herbert's current numbers make this the most counterintuitive offensive prediction: 937 passing yards, five touchdowns, seven interceptions and a 70.2 passer rating through five games. He has also absorbed 17 sacks. Against Denver, he managed 121 passing yards and was sacked five times. Receiving availability remains uncertain after Ladd McConkey dressed without playing, Quentin Johnston missed the game and Tre' Harris suffered a hamstring injury. Nevertheless, the prediction is that Herbert finally finds rhythm against a defense protecting a substantial lead. Two touchdown drives and a field goal produce 17 fourth-quarter points, forcing Kansas City to finish the game with its offense rather than coast. Walker provides that answer. The final forecast is Chiefs 38, Chargers 31: Kansas City remains unbeaten, but Los Angeles delivers a much stronger response than its record suggests. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Kansas City, but divisional familiarity and turnovers can make a comfortable matchup unpredictable. picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Chargers Preview: Kansas City Looks to Stay Undefeated Against Los Angeles - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers to advance to World Series TRENDING Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Photo by: David Brytus Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 8:27 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs return from their bye week looking to keep their perfect start alive when they host the Los Angeles Chargers in an important AFC West matchup on Sunday, October 18. Kansas City enters the game at 4-0 after winning its first four contests, while Los Angeles is searching for its first victory after opening the season 0-5. The Chargers will have a difficult challenge at Arrowhead Stadium as they try to turn their season around against one of the AFC's early standouts. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. Eastern on CBS. Patrick Mahomes Leads the Chiefs Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has helped Kansas City get off to an impressive start in 2026. Through four games, Mahomes has thrown for 1,037 yards and nine touchdowns with just two interceptions, giving the Chiefs a productive passing attack. Kansas City has also found success on the ground with running back Kenneth Walker III. Walker has rushed for 537 yards and four touchdowns, averaging 6.2 yards per carry. His ability to produce explosive runs has given opposing defenses another major concern beyond Mahomes. Head coach Andy Reid will look to keep that offensive balance going against a Chargers defense that has shown the ability to pressure quarterbacks. The Chiefs will also monitor wide receiver Rashee Rice, who missed practice Wednesday with a hamstring injury. Justin Herbert Faces a Difficult Challenge For Los Angeles, quarterback Justin Herbert needs to help an offense that has struggled to produce consistently. Herbert has thrown for 937 yards, five touchdowns and seven interceptions through five games. The Chargers have averaged only 16.8 points per game, making offensive improvement a major priority. Herbert has the arm talent to challenge Kansas City's secondary, but he will need better protection and consistent production from his receiving corps. Injuries have complicated that task, with several Los Angeles wide receivers and defensive starters appearing on the team's injury report this week. Head coach Jim Harbaugh must find a way to help his team limit mistakes and sustain drives. A stronger running game could ease the pressure on Herbert and help keep Mahomes off the field. Andy Reid vs. Jim Harbaugh The coaching matchup adds another layer to this divisional rivalry. Reid has Kansas City playing efficient football on both sides of the ball, while Harbaugh is trying to find answers after a difficult opening month. The Chargers swept the Chiefs in 2025, adding extra motivation for Kansas City to protect its home field and maintain control of the AFC West rivalry. A Critical AFC West Matchup Kansas City has an opportunity to improve to 5-0 and continue building momentum after its bye week. Los Angeles, meanwhile, needs a complete performance to avoid falling further behind in the division. Mahomes and Walker give the Chiefs multiple ways to attack, while Herbert will need to deliver a more consistent performance to help the Chargers compete. With the Chiefs chasing another strong start and the Chargers desperate to get their season moving, Sunday's matchup carries plenty of importance for both teams.

picks.headline: Chargers at Chiefs: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 6 game
picks.blurb: Opening lines: Spread: Chiefs -2.5 Moneyline: Chiefs -142; Chargers +120 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Chiefs vs Chargers expert picks Adam Kaufman: Chiefs 30, Chargers 13 A winless Chargers team visits a rested Patrick Mahomes. What could go wrong? Los Angeles keeps making life harder on itself with turnovers, penalties and injuries. Justin Herbert hasn't played well enough to overcome the problems around him, and Arrowhead isn't where I'd expect everything to suddenly click. Kansas City can lean on Kenneth Walker III without asking Mahomes to do all the heavy lifting. If the Chargers slow the run, there's still the small matter of defending the quarterback. I'm not blindly betting on an Andy Reid bye-week trend. I'm looking at two teams playing very different levels of football. The Chiefs take control early and leave the Chargers desperate for answers heading into their bye. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Chiefs 28, Chargers 17 Generating pressure has been a hassle for Kansas City's defense. Keeping Justin Herbert protected properly has been nearly impossible for Los Angeles. How each team fares on this front this week could prove telling in determining just how deep these issues go on both sides. But the chasm between one of the NFL's three remaining undefeated teams and one of its three winless teams remains wide, and taking on Patrick Mahomes and Co. on the road hardly seems like a get-right opportunity for Jim Harbaugh's crew. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Chiefs 34, Chargers 14 Let's play a game. Find a win on the Chargers' schedule. Week 11 against the Jets? They might be favored in that game at least. Week 13 against the Bucs? home.headline: GM shares more bad news for Tyreek Hill about potential return to NFL amid Chiefs rumors
home.blurb: GM shares more bad news for Tyreek Hill about potential return to NFL amid Chiefs rumors A recent report indicated that the Kansas City Chiefs and other NFL teams could pass on signing wide receiver Tyreek Hill amid fears that he could face a suspension after he admitted in a civil trial related to allegations of domestic violence that he "pushed" his estranged wife "against the wall" during an incident that occurred following their April 2025 separation. For a Casino.org article published on Tuesday, NFL insider Jason La Canfora spoke with one unnamed general manager who made it clear his club won't be signing Hill this fall. Tyreek Hill a "no-go" for at least one NFL team "He’s a no-go for us," that GM said about Hill. "Who’s going to sign him with the domestic stuff going on, and the (divorce) trial? No way. Nobody is going to pursue that, except maybe (Chiefs head coach Andy Reid)." Hill is still recovering from the gruesome knee injury he suffered while with the Miami Dolphins on Sept. 29, 2025, and it's believed he won't be ready to play before November at the earliest. Meanwhile, the Chiefs have been linked with pass-catchers since the summer, and Hill played under Reid from 2016 through the 2021 season. Chiefs could do more than just add Tyreek Hill? The Chiefs were previously mentioned as a potential landing spot for Marvin Harrison Jr. until the Arizona Cardinals traded him to the Houston Texans . Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Jerry Jeudy of the Cleveland Browns could also be options for the Chiefs before the trade deadline arrives on Nov. 10. "From what we gather," La Canfora explained, " the Chiefs are in the market to add more than one pass-catcher...Expect them to be as aggressive as any team in the league in terms of adding a playmaker on offense. They also have more of a stomach for players with significant off-field issues, including their former All-Pro receiver Tyreek Hill, who is trying to come back from injury at a time when he’s continued to have legal problems amid allegations of domestic violence." The 4-0 Chiefs are coming off their bye and will next host the 0-5 Los Angeles Chargers on Oct. 18. It remains to be seen whether Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes will get a new target before that game begins. As of Tuesday morning, DraftKings Sportsbook had the Chiefs as 8.5-point home favorites over the Chargers. Want more articles like this? The Houston Texans just got their first win. The Dallas Cowboys can't get out of their own way, and the Buffalo Bills are mauling everyone in their way. It's been a wacky start to the season, which has made our NFL picks and predictions for every game each week a bit more difficult than I expected. We're having to adjust our perceptions and expectations on the fly, and we're still in the mix as we head into what should be a fascinating Week 6. Zach Rotman came out of the bullpen for me last week and came through with a solid week. Many, many thanks to him for helping the cause, but I'm back in the saddle now. Let's hope I don't make this thing go any further off the rails, but let's dive right into this fun slate with our NFL picks for Week 6 as we make predictions both straight-up and against the spread for all 14 games on the slate this week. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 6 prediction to make Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Buffalo Bills at Las Vegas Raiders (+5.5) The Buffalo Bills have been rolling, including toppling the Rams in overtime in Los Angeles on Monday night. Stop me if you've heard this one before, but Buffalo has one of the NFL's best offenses behind Josh Allen and it doesn't seem like there's a defense in the league that's going to be able to stop this team from scoring 30 points - they're quite literally averaging 32.7 points per game after the first five games of the year. Meanwhile, the Raiders have certainly fallen back to earth a bit, losing two straight after their 3-0 start to the season. At the same time, the Bills defense is the same problem it's been for the past few years. It seems like Buffalo has to produce at this level offensively to win games because the defense is going to give it up. While the Raiders might not be a surprise contender, they still look like a quite competent football team behind Kirk Cousins and, while Buffalo will be able to score on their defense, they're still averaging 26.4 points per game on the year. I think Buffalo still has the offensive firepower against a middling defense to get the win in this game. But with it being in Vegas against a team that has a legitimate pulse, it's going to be another shootout and one that could likely be decided by a field goal once again. 5.5 points is a bit too many, so we'll take the Raiders against the spread and pray. Easiest NFL Week 6 pick on the board Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs (-8.5) This line could've been two touchdowns and I'm still taking the Kansas City Chiefs over the division rival Chargers. For starters, what has LA shown this season to make you believe they have a chance in Arrowhead in Week 6? No, seriously. There's been little evidence to think that this game will be close as the Chiefs have been absolutely rolling on both sides of the ball while Justin Herbert delivers the worst season of his career, the Chargers defense is middling at its best and the self-inflicted wounds in each game from LA multiply likes the heads of a hydra. If that weren't enough, Andy Reid is famously one of the most lethal head coaches when his team is coming off of the bye week. This isn't to say that the Chiefs are a perfect team as I maintain that they still need to find some more upgrades at wide receiver, especially after the gnarly Tyquan Thornton injury. While that may be true, though, they are a far better coached and more talented team than the winless Chargers and I wouldn't be surprised if this game was lopsided and out of hand early in favor of the home side. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dallas Cowboys (+1.5) at Green Bay Packers Coming off of a home loss to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels and the previously winless Buccaneers, naturally I'm taking the Dallas Cowboys to go on the road to Lambeau and beat the Packers as underdogs. What about this doesn't make sense to you? Yes, the optics look strange. However, this isn't about expecting the Cowboys hiring Mike Pettine to essentially help out new defensive coordinator Christian Parker drastically improving the defense, though it can't hurt. It's more about this being a likely shootout between these two teams because, despite what happened to Tyson Bagent and the Bears, I still don't trust Green Bay on that side of the ball. Furthermore, I also still don't trust the Packers run game, even against Dallas. Expect this game to go back and forth throughout the action, but I believe the Cowboys are going to have more offensive firepower and some adjustments on the side of the ball you can actually trust Dallas on to attack Green Bay throughout. They might not come up with many stops of their own, but they'll have enough to pull out the win. Plus, just from a narrative perspective, if ever there was a time for the Cowboys to keep their fans from abandoning ship, it's a game like this, and this franchise has been masterful at doing exactly that over the years. picks.blurb: Bills vs. Raiders Preview: Buffalo Looks to Keep Rolling Against Las Vegas - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers to advance to World Series TRENDING Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Bills vs. Raiders Preview: Buffalo Looks to Keep Rolling Against Las Vegas Photo by: Bob DeChiara Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 8:31 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Buffalo Bills head to Las Vegas on Sunday for a Week 6 matchup against the Raiders, with both teams looking to strengthen their positions in the AFC playoff race. Buffalo enters the game at 4-1 after an exciting 37-34 overtime victory over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night. The Raiders, meanwhile, are 3-2 after suffering a 45-17 loss to the New England Patriots. With the Bills carrying one of the league's most productive offenses and Las Vegas looking to bounce back, Sunday's matchup at Allegiant Stadium presents an important test for both teams. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. Eastern on CBS. Josh Allen Leads Buffalo's Explosive Offense Quarterback Josh Allen remains the centerpiece of Buffalo's offense. Through five games, Allen has thrown for 1,249 yards and seven touchdowns while adding eight rushing touchdowns. His ability to create plays with both his arm and legs makes him one of the most difficult quarterbacks to defend. Allen was particularly dangerous against the Rams, throwing for 342 yards and two touchdowns while rushing for 121 yards. His performance helped Buffalo survive a back-and-forth contest and improve to 4-1. Running back James Cook has also been productive, rushing for 532 yards through five games. His speed and ability to create explosive plays give the Bills another weapon that Las Vegas must account for. Head coach Joe Brady will look to keep the offense balanced while helping Allen avoid costly turnovers. Buffalo has committed nine giveaways over its last three games, making ball security an important focus heading into Sunday. Raiders Need a Strong Response Las Vegas will look to quarterback Kirk Cousins to help the offense recover from its disappointing performance against New England. Cousins has thrown for 1,269 yards and 12 touchdowns through five games, giving the Raiders a capable passing attack. Tight end Brock Bowers has been one of Cousins' primary targets, recording 312 receiving yards and three touchdowns. His ability to create mismatches could be especially important against a Buffalo defense that has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks. The Raiders will also rely on running back Ashton Jeanty , who has rushed for 291 yards this season. Establishing the ground game could help Las Vegas control possession and prevent Allen from spending too much time on the field. Head coach Klint Kubiak will need his team to improve its offensive line play and limit mistakes after the loss to New England. A Major Test for Both Teams Buffalo enters the matchup averaging 32.8 points per game, while Las Vegas has averaged 26.4. Both defenses have experienced difficulties, creating opportunities for the offenses to make an impact. The Bills will try to maintain their momentum after the overtime win, while the Raiders need a response at home to remain competitive in the AFC West. With Allen's dual threat ability, Cousins' passing production and two offenses looking to establish control, Sunday's matchup could be an important measuring stick for both teams as the NFL season continues.

picks.headline: Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6
picks.blurb: Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers to advance to World Series TRENDING Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 Tim Crean, ClutchPoints Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:44 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Buffalo Bills face off against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. This matchup between the 4-1 Bills and the 3-2 Raiders gets a prime spot in the late Sunday window as one of the best games of the week. These two original AFC franchises haven't played a game with meaningful stakes for both teams since the 1993 "Just Freeze Baby" Divisional Round game . Now, as both sides come into this game with winning records, let's make some bold Bills-Raiders predictions. Start your Raiders in fantasy football The Bills are their own worst enemy so far this season, as they love to gift their opponents chances to stay in the game. Whether it is shockingly cavalier Josh Allen interceptions, infuriating James Cook fumbles, or the fact that the defense (outside of Deone Walker and Gregory Rousseau) looks like it has no clue what it is doing right now, Buffalo loves keeping the other team in the game. Sunday will be no different, as fans should expect at least two turnovers from the Bills' offense and long stretches where the Raiders' O looks like the 2007 New England Patriots. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) That means big games from the Raiders' defense, Kirk Cousins, Brock Bowers, Ashton Jeanty, and maybe even the likes of Mike Washington Jr., Michael Mayer, and Tre Tucker. So, for all you fantasy football players out there, any Raiders on your roster should be a good play in Week 6 . Josh Allen delivers again Despite the mediocre (or worse) play at times from the Bills' offensive line, wide receivers, tight end, and running backs, and defensive back seven, the Bills are 4-1 and leading the AFC East thanks to one man: Brandon Beane. Just kidding! He's the reason the rest of the team is struggling so much. The real reason is Josh Allen. Through five weeks, Allen is still the betting favorite for NFL MVP this year. Yes, Brock Bowers is playing great, and Patrick Mahomes is back, but if you define MVP as the players whose absence would tank his team's chances the most, Allen has to be the answer. Monday night's dramatic OT win over the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams came courtesy of 210 yards passing and a staggering 121 yards rushing from the Bills QB. Sure, he threw his obligatory head-scratching pick in the first half, but in the second, it was a one-man battle with 53 Rams players, and the singular man won. Against the Raiders, expect more of the same. Vegas has an improved defense this season and an incredible pass rusher in Maxx Crosby, but that only means Allen will be forced to take off even more as usual. And with his receivers getting minimal separation and Cook's suspect ball security, it will be all Allen, all the time in Week 6. Bills 31, Raiders 24 This won't be a cakewalk for the Bills by any means, as the Raiders are one of (if not) the most improved teams in the league. We know Cousins is a professional QB, the Raiders have some incredible young offensive weapons, and Klint Kubiak seems like a legit NFL head coach with an incredibly bright future. Allen doesn't have those last two things, as his skill position core is the exact same as last year, as long as D.J. Moore is out injured and his "new" head coach is just the same offensive coordinator who couldn't get it done the past three seasons, but with a more impressive title. Nevertheless, Allen should be able to will his Bills to victory over the Raiders in Week 6 just by sheer force of talent and will. As good as Las Vegas has looked at times this season, they are probably a year or two away from being legit contenders. That's why we'll take the Buffalo to win here, and to do so by slightly more than the -5.5-point spread suggests. picks.headline: Week 6 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Cowboys and Packers had much different results last week
picks.blurb: Week 6 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Cowboys and Packers had much different results last week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers sweep Dodgers to advance to World Series TRENDING Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT WNBA All-Defensive first team Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 15, 2026 at 2:37 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads One week can change the entire perception of an NFL team — sometimes that's good, sometimes it's not. The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers were both 2-2 coming into last week's games. The Cowboys weren't considered a Super Bowl contender, but they were at least looking OK — especially in a bad NFC East — with a home game against the winless Buccaneers coming up. The Packers had played so poorly through four weeks that they were home underdogs to the Bears for the first time in 20 years , even though Chicago was starting its backup quarterback. The Cowboys and Packers come into Week 6's Sunday night game with their seasons flipped around. The Cowboys looked horrible against the Buccaneers, losing to an undrafted rookie quarterback in Jalon Daniels. The defensive problems finally got to a point in which the Cowboys hired longtime NFL defensive coordinator Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant and said defensive coordinator Christian Parker will now call plays from the press box. There's always some angst in Dallas because of the attention on the Cowboys all the time, but it's not like the defensive problems are made up. Dallas was last in defensive DVOA last season and they're last so far this season. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Meanwhile, the talk of Matt LaFleur being on the hot seat seems like it was a lot longer than a week ago. The best way to gain back the confidence of Packers fans is to blow out the Bears, and the Packers did just that. They blasted Chicago, 31-7, with Jordan Love embarrassing the Bears defense with his deep passing and Green Bay shutting down everything Chicago's offense wanted to do. After not playing a good game through four weeks, the Packers played a great game in Week 5. That makes Week 6 hard to figure out. Do the Cowboys rebound or is the defense simply unfixable? What's the real Packers team — the one that couldn't run the ball, couldn't protect Love and had a below-average defense through four games, or the one we saw Sunday? The Packers are small favorites Sunday night, indicating the oddsmakers don't have a lot of confidence in them still. But it's tougher to bank on the Cowboys' defense. Packers -1.5 is the pick , though it could all look different for both teams next week. That's how the NFL goes. The Green Bay Packers' MarShawn Lloyd celebrates a touchdown with the fans at Lambeau Field last week. (AP Photo/Nam Huh) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 6 of the NFL season: Seahawks (-2.5) over Broncos Not all is great for the defending champs, who can't run the ball and still don't have an offensive option other than Jaxon Smith-Njigba. But they've been far better than the Broncos, who were on their way to losing to the winless and injury-plagued Chargers before saving themselves with a fourth-quarter rally. The matchup of Seattle's defense against an aimless Broncos offense is enough to take the Seahawks. Jaguars (-2.5) over Texans A bit of a weird line. The Jaguars are 4-1 and while last week's miracle win over the Eagles wasn't great, they do look like a legitimate contender in the AFC. The Texans are 1-4 and their lone win came against the 0-5 Titans. And yet, in a neutral site game — if either team has the edge it's Jacksonville, who does the London trip every season and stayed overseas after playing there last week — the Jaguars aren't even giving a full field goal. Yes it's a desperate Houston team with a very good defense, but it's not a lot of respect for the Jaguars. Falcons (+1.5) over Bears It appears Michael Penix Jr. and Caleb Williams will start, which should make for an entertaining game. The big question for this one will be what to make of the Bears defense. In Week 1 and 5 they gave up 68 combined points. From Weeks 2-4 they allowed 28 points. The hot stretch in the middle could have come from facing three bad offenses (Vikings without Kyler Murray in bad weather, Eagles, Jets) instead of the Panthers and Packers, their other two opponents who both scored more than 30 points. The Falcons are a good offense with Penix, so points should be coming. Browns (+5.5) over Ravens The Ravens should have confidence after beating the Falcons without Lamar Jackson last week. However, a Tyler Huntley offense still isn't one I'm comfortable laying 5.5 points with on the road. Buccaneers (+2.5) over Steelers Metrics like DVOA and net EPA per play say these teams are practically even. The Buccaneers have the rest advantage, having played last Thursday night, and the Steelers are 0-2 on the road (3-0 at home). Daniels could be exposed by the best defense he's faced, but it's also not the intimidating Steelers defense from recent years. Patriots (-7.5) over Jets The Patriots are officially warmed up. The start to the season was lackluster, but Drake Maye is coming off two good games in a row. The Jets are better than some expected, but they're facing a team that has its season back on track and wants to keep that going. Bet the New England Patriots to cover the spread at sportsbooks Giants (+1.5) over Saints It's hard to buy the Giants. There's no evidence they're a good team despite their 3-1-1 record. But it's not like there are any signs that the Saints are much better. New Orleans is 30th in DVOA ahead of only the hopeless Titans and Dolphins. Anything can happen when Jameis Winston is starting at quarterback, good or bad — good luck predicting it. Panthers (-1) over Eagles It's weird to see the Panthers favored at Philadelphia (though some books have the Eagles as a small favorite). But to this point, Carolina has been the far better team. Also, they're coming off a bye while the Eagles come right off a flight from London, where they took a horrific loss after kicking a go-ahead field goal with eight seconds left. Colts (-7) over Titans The Titans should be very happy the Dolphins exist, or else there would be even more talk about how bad they are. Indianapolis hasn't been great, either, but it's just too difficult to take the Titans right now. Cardinals (+12.5) over Rams It's quite possible the Rams take out their frustrations on the Cardinals. Los Angeles is 2-3, but the schedule has been tough and it starts to ease up with a game against Arizona, which just got throttled by the Lions. The Cardinals seem to be running out of steam after looking decent to start the season. Still, 12.5 points is a lot considering the Rams haven't looked great yet, and Arizona can move the ball, especially in garbage time. Raiders (+5.5) over Bills The Bills are coming off an emotional, difficult overtime win against the Rams on Monday night. They are the better team, but that's a tough situational spot, and the Raiders are not as bad as they looked last week against the Patriots. Let's give Vegas one more shot to show that 3-0 start wasn't fraudulent. Chiefs (-8) over Chargers The Chargers aren't just bad, they're injured. They held their own against the Broncos last week, but that probably says more about Denver. This season is already ugly for Los Angeles and it's not going to get much better. Commanders (+7.5) over 49ers If the Commanders aren't completely downtrodden after one of the dumbest endings in recent NFL history last week, in which they casually watched the final minute of overtime run out without getting a field-goal attempt, then this seems like too many points. The 49ers have played very well on both sides of the ball (the defense has been a great surprise), but there is some danger of a letdown after winning at Seattle. Take the points and hope last week's fiasco doesn't still linger for Washington. Last week: 5-9-1 Season to date: 34-43-2

away.blurb: Now, to add insult to injury, the NFL is punishing two Cowboys players for their actions in Week 4 of the NFL season. NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Brewers sweep Dodgers to advance to World Series NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week Anne Erickson Sat, October 10, 2026 at 9:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Dallas Cowboys fell 24-16 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on "Thursday Night Football" to kick off the NFL's Week 5 festivities, and it wasn't a good look for the franchise. The main reason this loss was rough is because the Cowboys fell to a 0-4 Buccaneers team that has undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels subbing for the injured Baker Mayfield. away.headline: Dallas Cowboys Could Bench DaRon Bland to Avoid Paying Massive Injury Guarantees
away.blurb: As pointed out by ESPN's Bill Barnwell, the Cowboys would be in a frustrating financial hole if Bland were to suffer an injury this season. "The Cowboys don't want to be on the hook for that money, so it would hardly be a surprise if they took Bland out of the lineup altogether once (Cobie) Durant and (Joey) Porter Jr. are back on the field to avoid triggering those guarantees, which would happen if Bland suffers a significant injury," Barnwell wrote. The Cowboys are also still figuring out exactly what they have in Shavon Revel Jr., who impressed during training camp but has had his own share of struggles this season. From being a fifth-round pick to making NFL history, Dallas Cowboys cornerback DaRon Bland deserves a ton of credit for the career he's made for himself. However, the magic from his record-setting 2023 season has quickly faded. Despite signing a four-year, $90 million contract extension last August, Bland has become a liability this season on a Dallas defense that already has enough problems to deal with. Bland hasn't had an interception since Week 7 of last season. And if he's not jumping routes and running it back for a touchdown -- something he's done six times in his career -- Bland is getting burned down the field for huge gains. As a result of his fading production and hefty contract, the Cowboys face an interesting dilemma when it comes to how they handle Bland's involvement in the defense moving forward in order to help themselves both on the field and in the bank. Cowboys Would Owe DaRon Bland $13 Million Due to Injury Dallas would owe Bland $13 million in guaranteed money if he suffers "a significant injury." Should he stay healthy, the Cowboys would avoid having to pay up. This situation makes it perfectly reasonable for the Cowboys to bench Bland moving forward. Until he proves he can produce at the level that his contract commands, Dallas faces a lose-lose situation: continue to suffer on defense while running the risk of owing Bland millions in injury guarantees. If the Cowboys are going to be awful on defense, they might as well do it with cornerbacks that won't put them in a tough spot financially. Cowboys Have More Reasonable Options to Work With When everyone is healthy, Dallas has multiple options that certainly feel like an upgrade from the current version of Bland. The Cowboys signed former Los Angeles Rams cornerback Cobie Durant this season before making the blockbuster deal for former Pittsburgh Steelers star Joey Porter Jr. earlier this month. And on top of that, Dallas has versatile defensive back Caleb Downs, who brings a bit of everything as a slot corner or a safety. It's hard to imagine Bland being outright ruled inactive for Week 6's matchup against the Green Bay Packers but the Cowboys could certainly benefit by slowing decreasing his snap count as the season goes on. The biggest problem the Commanders will have is Mike Evans. That's not a deep analysis. It's something every team faces when playing the 49ers. Purdy said Evans makes a big difference , according to ESPN. "He's a game changer," Purdy said after the win over the Seahawks. "True X receiver that, if you get the right look and stuff and you give him a chance, he can make defenses pay. "I thought today he did a great job with that, going up and getting the ball multiple times and just using his length and everything to create some separation. So as a quarterback, any time I have an (opportunity) to go to him, it always feels good." Evans doesn't shy away from the attention. And why should he? He's a future Hall of Famer. "I do feel like I'm one of the best receivers in the game," Evans said. "I got a big frame, so if you throw it around me, I'm going to do my best to try to make those contested grabs." The 49ers won't have Deebo Samuel, who suffered a hamstring injury against the Seahawks. That could allow the Commanders to focus more attention on Evans. But the 49ers still have threats, including George Kittle. And even Kittle has major respect for Evans, according to a post on X. "Mike Evans is really good at football," Kittle posted. 49ers TE George Kittle will have a season-high reception total Kittle's best game came in Week 3 against the Cardinals as he grabbed six passes for 82 yards and a pair of scores. Look for him to have a similar line against the Commanders with Samuel on the shelf. The 49ers have Kittle, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, and Jacob Cowing on the roster. And that's enough , said head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to ESPN. "I think we have enough," Shanahan said. "We've got three guys on practice squad also who can help. I mean, anytime you lose this number of guys, whether it's four guys or five guys, whatever it is, it's a huge challenge. But we do have guys in this building who can do it, and we'll always look." Commanders QB Jayden Daniels will finally cross 200-yard passing mark In three games this season, Daniels hasn't totaled over 200 yards passing. Look for that to change against the 49ers. It makes sense for the 49ers to focus defensively on keeping Daniels in check as a runner. He's coming off a game where he ran for 103 yards on nine carries and a pair of touchdowns. And look for the Commanders' game plan to lean more on the passing game than it has so far this season. Part of it will likely be from necessity as the Commanders figure to be chasing points throughout this game. Daniels has a lot to prove after his late-game blunder against the Giants. He has tried to own the situation , according to ESPN. "We have to stop the clock," Daniels said. "We have to know the situation. We have to relay that as an offense. It starts with everyone, top down. Ultimately, it's on me." A bounce-back game against the 49ers by Daniels won't help Quinn's future as head coach. But it would be an olive branch to Commanders' fans who are furious about Daniels' mental meltdown. Commanders WR Terry McLaurin will get a long TD Look for the Commanders to strike deep against the 49ers. McLaurin should be the beneficiary with a 40-plus-yard score. McLaurin hasn't been anything special from a fantasy perspective this season. He had catch totals of 2, 2, 6, and 4 in his first four games. He has 203 total yards and one touchdown. Those aren't WR1 numbers. He is playing like a pedestrian blob so far this season. And while he probably won't juice up those numbers much against the 49ers' tough defense, it's not out of the realm of possibility for him to get a deep ball. How big of an ask is a 40-yard TD strike between Daniels and McLaurin? Consider that Daniels' longest pass of the season is 33 yards. McLaurin's longest catch is 30 yards. Those numbers seem to belie the likelihood of a long hookup. However, the 49ers can't fear the deep ball because of this duo's modest production. And that's why there's a window of opportunity for a bomb. However, look for the Commanders to fall to 1-4-1 after this one. They don't have the roster to compete with the 49ers. away.headline: Commanders vs. 49ers Thursday injury report: Bill Croskey-Merritt not practicing
away.blurb: Commanders running back Bill Croskey-Merritt had his best game of this early season on Sunday, turning in 82 yards and a touchdown on just 11 carries. His high per carry average was boosted by an explosive touchdown, but Croskey-Merritt came out of Sunday’s 27-27 draw with the New York Giants a bit banged up. Also, Austin Ekeler is dealing with a chest injury and was seen by on-site reporters wearing a non-contact jersey. He was formally limited in practice. The Commanders also practiced without receiver Stefon Diggs and safeties Percy Butler and Tyler Owens, who are all dealing with hamstring injuries. Those guys could return to work later in the week. Defensive lineman Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral) was also out on Thursday. Defensive lineman Charles Omenihu (groin) and quarterback Marcus Mariota (knee) remained out of practice but were seen by reporters working off to the side . S Nick Cross – Listed with an illness. Was hospitalized for internal injuries in Dallas after the game. Ruled out for Sunday after not traveling to London He did not participate in Thursday’s practice with a groin injury, per the Commanders. Head coach Dan Quinn didn’t address the issue during his press conference earlier in the day, so clarity on Croskey-Merritt might not come until Saturday or even beyond. Quinn said that safety Nick Cross (illness), cornerback Trey Amos (ankle) and running back Jeremy McNichols — the later two are on injured reserve — are expected to be full participants in practice this week. away.headline: Commanders news: Backfield concerns grow; 49ers await Nick Bosa update | Burgundy roundup
away.blurb: - Thursday brought another running back concern for Washington, and this one involves the guy who just rushed for 82 yards and a touchdown against the Giants . Jacory Croskey-Merritt missed practice with a groin injury, while Austin Ekeler was limited with a chest issue. With Kaytron Allen now in Miami and Robert Henry Jr. in Seattle, the timing isn't great for a Commanders backfield that's been changing almost every week. - The undefeated 49ers have been dealing with receiver injuries themselves, although some help could be on the way. Christian Kirk was back on the practice field Thursday after San Francisco opened his 21-day return window, participating on a limited basis for the first time since being sidelined with a calf injury during training camp. He still needs to be activated before playing against Washington. The 49ers also promoted defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo to the active roster and signed linebacker Eugene Asante to their practice squad. - At least Washington had some encouraging news on its own injury report. Linebacker Jordan Magee had his return-to-practice window opened after spending time on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, and Trey Amos, Nick Cross, and Jeremy McNichols were all full participants Thursday. Magee was limited, but considering how many players the Commanders have had unavailable through five games, having some of those names working their way back is a welcome change. - Speaking of injuries, San Francisco had a few more notable names missing practice Thursday, including Nick Bosa (calf), Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles), and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). away.headline: Commanders' injury report gives Giants a leg up in Week 5, even with Jayden Daniels
away.blurb: In fact, Big Blue might be the healthier team on Sunday. The Washington Commanders are dealing with a long list of injuries, even with Jayden Daniels likely set to return to the field. His teammates, on the other hand, have not had such an encouraging week. His top two receivers, Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs, did not participate in practice on Wednesday or Thursday. McLaurin participated in a limited capacity on Friday, but Diggs did not. Both wideouts are dealing with hamstring injuries. If McLaurin and Diggs are both out, Washington will be left with Dyami Brown, Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, and Luke McCaffrey as its only healthy receivers. Commanders' injury report gives Giants a leg up in Week 5, even with Jayden Daniels Skip to main content News It may feel like the New York Giants are the most injured team in the NFL. They are not. Losing Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns, among others, for the season was a devastating blow, but the G-Men still have enough healthy talent on both sides of the ball to remain competitive, especially in a wide-open NFC East. With key commanders missing from the lineup, the Giants have an important advantage in what has become a crucial game in the NFC East title race. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs headline Commanders' injury report vs. Giants Daniels was a full participant in Commanders practice on both Wednesday and Thursday. Barring an unexpected change over the weekend, he should be able to play for the first time since injuring his elbow in Week 2. Of course, the Giants have some important injuries of their own. Braxton Berrios is now set to miss the season with a foot injury. Chauncey Golston's neck injury could leave New York thin on the edge, and safety Jason Pinnock is dealing with a concussion. But in terms of new names popping up on the injury report, the Giants certainly have the advantage in this game. Commanders' injury report gives Giants a clear advantage in Week 5 The Giants' secondary hasn't been stellar this season. The pass defense has been average in most categories and has been torn apart by the most efficient passing offenses it has faced. But if Washington is without its top two wide receivers, New York's secondary should be able to take control of the game. Deonte Banks, who has been a full participant in practice this week , and Greg Newsome II can lock Brown and Burks down on the outside while Dru Phillips handles Williams in the slot. If the Giants limit the Commanders' rushing attack, which hasn't been particularly efficient this year, they can put this game away early.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , veteran receiver Christian Kirk is having his practice window opened, meaning the 49ers might finally be getting a WR back from injury this season. 49ers open practice window for WR Christian Kirk "49ers opened the practice window for WR Christian Kirk, who has been on injured reserve all season due to a calf injury," Schefter reports. home.headline: Super Bowl stock report for NFL Week 6: 49ers emerge as new favorites, Bears await Caleb Williams' return
home.blurb: Super Bowl stock report for NFL Week 6: 49ers emerge as new favorites, Bears await Caleb Williams' return - CBS Sports site: media | arena: nfl | pageType: stories | section: | slug: super-bowl-stock-report-for-nfl-week-6 | sport: football | route: article_single.us | 6-keys: media/spln/nfl/reg/free/stories Skip to Main Content Close Menu All Sports Menu Sports Watch Fantasy Betting Featured NFL User Menu Settings Log Out Log In Sign Up Fantasy & Games See All ArrowForward # # LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Perhaps their seemingly never-ending ailments will catch up to them again, but the same could be said for any team in the league. It is time to simply enjoy what the 49ers are doing and stop worrying about their ability to stay healthy. Frankly, they might just win the Super Bowl regardless of who is available. Through five weeks, it feels like their year. Here is how the rest of the Super Bowl race shakes out as the season approaches Week 6. Stock down: Bears desperately await Caleb Williams' return Would the Chicago Bears be 5-0 if Caleb Williams did not get hurt in Week 2? Suppose he stays on the field for that critical fourth-quarter drive in the 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. He would have had at least two more looks at the end zone. If he were available in Week 5, the Bears probably would not throw three interceptions in a 31-7 rout at the hands of the bitter rival Green Bay Packers . That is all hypothetical, of course, but Williams' talent makes it fair to wonder. Instead, the Bears are two games back of the NFC North lead and stand in the middle of the conference's slog of three-win teams. They seek a rebound effort on the heels of the second-worst loss of Ben Johnson's head coaching career. That will be harder to obtain with edge rusher Montez Sweat out for two games for a violation of the NFL's performance-enhancing substances policy . The good news (and Chicago needs some right now) is that Williams is on track to play in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons . His hamstring strain is behind him, which cleared the way for a return to practice on Wednesday. Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent kept the ship afloat but had clear limitations — most notably in the frustrating loss to the Packers — whereas Williams seems to be blossoming into a top-tier quarterback capable of leading his team deep into the postseason. It was easy to sneer at the Pittsburgh Steelers in the offseason when they hired a past-his-prime coach, let Aaron Rodgers drag them along with his decision-making process as to whether to return for another year and got embarrassed by the Philadelphia Eagles on draft day. They say everything happens for a reason, and they might be onto something when it comes to the Steelers. All of those developments, somehow, seem to have played out perfectly.
